topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Cervical Nerve Root Shoulder Scapula (Biomedical Sciences)
question: A patient comes in with neck injury from an accident. He has pain and limited range of motion in his shoulders and scapula. Which nerve root was affected during the accident?
explanation: The C5 nerve root innervates key muscles of the shoulder and scapula (deltoid, rotator cuff, rhomboids). Injury to C5 commonly causes pain and limited ROM in these areas following neck trauma.

topic: Risk Management & Safety - Infant CPR Responsiveness Check (Biomedical Sciences)
question: The first step when performing CPR on babies is to ____________________.
options: Shake the baby and see if they respond
Tap the shoulders and pat the feet
correct: Tap the shoulders and pat the feet
explanation: The first step in infant CPR is to check responsiveness by gently tapping the shoulders and patting the feet while calling the infant. Shaking is dangerous and can cause injury.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Hematopoiesis White Blood Cells Origin (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Stem cells responsible for the production of the majority of white blood cells originate in the:
explanation: Hematopoietic stem cells in the red bone marrow produce the majority of white blood cells (as well as RBCs and platelets) in adults.

topic: Infection Control - Highest Hepatitis Exposure Risk Period (Biomedical Sciences)
question: The period of greatest risk of exposure to Hepatitis for healthcare workers is:
options: One year after start of professional practice
Three years after start of professional practice
Two years after start of professional practice
explanation: Healthcare students and new trainees have the highest risk of needlestick injuries and bloodborne pathogen (Hepatitis) exposure due to inexperience with procedures and safety protocols.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Renin-Angiotensin System ACE Location (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Where is angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) made?
explanation: Angiotensin Converting Enzyme (ACE) is primarily produced in the endothelial cells of the lungs. It converts angiotensin I to angiotensin II, a key step in blood pressure regulation.

topic: Reporting & Record-Keeping - Purpose of Medical Records (Biomedical Sciences)
question: All of the following are true about patient medical records, EXCEPT:
options: A source of information about communicable diseases
explanation: Medical records do have legal value, but that’s not their primary role. That’s why this is the best answer to the “EXCEPT” format. The key to this question is the wording. Primary a legal document. Medical records are primarily medical records and then if needed a legal document that will hold up in court.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Orthostatic Blood Pressure Measurement (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Which of the following is the correct way to check standing blood pressure?
options: Have the patient lie in supine position for 3-10 minutes. Have the patient stand up. Check the blood pressure within 3 minutes of the patient standing up.
Have the patient lie in supine position until the heart rate slows. Have the patient stand up. Check the blood pressure after the patient stands for 2 minutes.

Have the patient lie in supine position for up to 3 minutes. Have the patient stand up. Check the blood pressure within the first minute. Check the blood pressure after the patient stands for 3 minutes.
Have the patient lie in supine position for more than 10 minutes. Have the patient stand up. Check the blood pressure after the patient stands for more than 5 minutes.
correct: Have the patient lie in supine position for up to 3 minutes. Have the patient stand up. Check the blood pressure within the first minute. Check the blood pressure after the patient stands for 3 minutes.
explanation: Have the patient lie in supine position for up to 3 minutes. Have the patient stand up. Check the blood pressure within the first minute. Check the blood pressure after the patient stands for 3 minutes.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Autonomic Nervous System Pupil & Heart Rate (Biomedical Sciences)
question: ______________ is responsible for pupil constriction and slow heartbeat (bradycardia). _____________ is responsible for pupil dilation and fast heartbeat (tachycardia) and also reduced saliva and digestive fluids.
explanation: The parasympathetic nervous system causes pupil constriction and bradycardia (rest-and-digest). The sympathetic nervous system causes pupil dilation, tachycardia, and reduced saliva/digestion (fight-or-flight).

topic: Biomedical Sciences - ARDS Causes (Biomedical Sciences)
question: All of the following, except __________________, can cause Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
explanation: ARDS can be caused by pneumonia, aspiration of water/gastric contents, and toxic inhalants. Asthma is an obstructive airway disease and does not cause ARDS.

topic: Pharmacology - ACE Inhibitors Side Effects (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Which is NOT a side-effect of Capoten (Captopril)?
explanation: Captopril commonly causes dry cough, orthostatic hypotension, and proteinuria. It typically causes decreased or altered taste (dysgeusia), not increased taste.

topic: Infection Control - Hepatitis Vaccines (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Vaccines are available for which of the following types of hepatitis?
explanation: Vaccines are currently available for Hepatitis A and Hepatitis B. There is no vaccine for Hepatitis C or D.

topic: Decision-Making & Standard of Care - Referral for Suspected Shingles (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Sarah, age 74, recently moved into an assisted living facility. She is in your office today complaining of a red rash on her arm. She says it started on the back of her hand along the LI line and is now traveling up the arm. What is the appropriate next step you should take?
options: Call an ambulance to take her to the ER
Refer her to her primary doctor
Refer her to a dermatologist that you know who is very good but won't be able to see her for at least two weeks
correct: Refer her to her primary doctor
explanation: A unilateral dermatomal rash traveling up the arm in an elderly patient suggests shingles (herpes zoster). Prompt referral to primary doctor allows early antiviral treatment and prevents complications.

topic: Reporting & Record-Keeping - State Licensing Board Access to Records (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Your patient complains to your state’s acupuncture board about an incident that happened during their appointment in your clinic. The state licensing body demands a copy of the patient’s medical records for review of the care you provided. Do state licensing bodies have the right to assess patient medical records?
options: It will depend on the state you are practicing in.
Licensing bodies must have a search warrant signed by a judge.
Yes, all state licensing bodies in all 51 states and US territories have the right to access patient medical records.
Licensing bodies can never access your patient records.
correct: It will depend on the state you are practicing in.
explanation: State licensing boards have authority to investigate complaints, but the specific rules and processes for accessing patient records can vary by state. Always follow your state’s regulations.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Lumbar Vertebrae & Rib Landmark (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Which of the following lumbar vertebrae is located level with the free end of the 12th rib?
explanation: The free end of the 12th rib corresponds to the level of the L1 (first lumbar) vertebra per the question bank.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Rheumatoid Arthritis Common Sites (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Which of the following is not a common location for rheumatoid arthritis to present?
explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis typically presents in the hands (MCP/PIP joints), wrists, knees, and elbows. Hip involvement usually occurs later in the disease course.

topic: Infection Control - Hand Hygiene in Clinic (Biomedical Sciences)
question: For handwashing in clinic, which of the following is recommended?
explanation: According to the question bank, liquid soap and water is the recommended method for handwashing in the clinic.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Digestive Enzymes Salivary Amylase (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Salivary amylase is made by the salivary glands and is used to break down ________ when you chew your food.
explanation: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) is produced by the salivary glands and begins the digestion of starch (carbohydrates) into simpler sugars in the mouth.

topic: Decision-Making & Standard of Care - Red Flags Amenorrhea + Bleeding (Biomedical Sciences)
question: You haven’t seen your patient in some time. She comes in because she hasn’t had a period in 12 weeks (3 months). Today she started having heavy uterine bleeding accompanied by fainting, nausea, and vomiting. She has a history of amenorrhea. What should you rule out?
explanation: A patient with amenorrhea followed by sudden heavy bleeding, fainting, nausea, and vomiting must have ectopic pregnancy ruled out immediately — this is a medical emergency that can cause life-threatening internal bleeding.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Menstrual Cycle Hormone Changes (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Estrogen increases during which two phases of the menstrual cycle?
explanation: Estrogen levels rise during the follicular phase as follicles develop and reach their peak during the ovulatory phase to trigger ovulation.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Cardiovascular Risk Factors Lipids (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Which of the following is the greatest risk factor for heart disease?
explanation: Low HDL (“good” cholesterol) combined with high LDL (“bad” cholesterol) is the lipid profile that carries the highest risk for developing heart disease.

topic: Risk Management & Safety - Emergency Response Respiratory Arrest (Biomedical Sciences)
question: You are out on a walk with your friend and find a person lying on the side walk. She has a pulse but is not breathing. What is the first thing you should do?
explanation: In a person with a pulse but not breathing (respiratory arrest), the first priority is to call 911 / activate emergency services immediately. Rescue breathing should follow.

topic: Infection Control - Disinfection Protocols Bleach Solution (Biomedical Sciences)
question: When using a diluted bleach solution in clinic, the solution should not be more than _______ hours old.
explanation: Diluted bleach solution loses potency over time. Standard infection control guidelines recommend preparing fresh solution and using it within 24 hours.

topic: Pharmacology - Respiratory Medications (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Singulair (montelukast) is used for which of the following conditions?
explanation: Singulair (montelukast) is a leukotriene receptor antagonist primarily used for the maintenance treatment of asthma and prevention of exercise-induced bronchoconstriction.

topic: Infection Control - MRSA Colonization Rates (Biomedical Sciences)
question: What population may be carriers of MRSA (Methicillin Resistant Staphylococcous Aureus)?
explanation: According to the question bank, 1 in 10 people may be carriers of MRSA. (Note: Broader medical sources often cite ~1 in 3 people as carriers; we follow the question bank for exam preparation.)

topic: Biomedical Sciences - BMI Healthy Range (Biomedical Sciences)
question: When measuring a person’s body mass index, a health weight is BMI between _______.
explanation: A healthy BMI range is generally 18.5–24.9. Among the options, 19–25 is the best match for a healthy weight.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Musculoskeletal Scapular Winging (Biomedical Sciences)
question: While evaluating a patient, the doctor notices that the patient’s scapula seems to protrude forward on one side. What muscle could be damaged?
explanation: The serratus anterior muscle keeps the scapula flat against the rib cage. Weakness or damage to this muscle causes “winged scapula,” where the scapula protrudes forward.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Endocrinology Thyroid Function Tests (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Elevated TSH levels would be seen in a patient with:
explanation: In primary hypothyroidism, the thyroid gland is underactive, so the pituitary releases more TSH to try to stimulate it. TSH is therefore elevated. In hyperthyroidism (including Graves’ disease), TSH is usually low.

topic: Pharmacology - Antibiotics Indications (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Sarah was prescribed Levaquin (levofloxacin) by her doctor. What condition does she have?
explanation: Levaquin (levofloxacin) is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections such as bacterial pneumonia. It is not effective against viral infections.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Thyroid Disorders Diagnostics (Biomedical Sciences)
question: For confirming a diagnosis of Hashimoto’s thyroiditis, all of the following labs are tested, except?
explanation: Diagnosis of Hashimoto’s thyroiditis is confirmed with elevated TSH, low T4, and positive thyroid autoantibodies (especially anti-TPO). Total or Free T3 is not necessary for confirmation.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Rheumatology Rheumatoid Nodules (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Patient complains of firm, non-tender nodules that are not attached to overlying skin. They are attached to the underlying periosteum. They are slightly distal to the olecranon bursa. Your most likely diagnosis is:
explanation: Rheumatoid nodules are firm, non-tender, subcutaneous nodules often attached to periosteum or tendons. They commonly appear near the olecranon (elbow area) and are a classic extra-articular feature of rheumatoid arthritis.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Cardiac Anatomy Heart Apex (Biomedical Sciences)
question: The heart apex is located at which ICS?
explanation: The apex of the heart is normally located at the 5th intercostal space (ICS) in the mid-clavicular line on the left side. This is the usual location of the point of maximal impulse (PMI).

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Infectious Diseases STI Trichomoniasis (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Siara is 3 months pregnant. She has just come from the doctor who diagnosed her with trichomoniasis vaginitis. What symptoms would you expect to see?
options: Painful blisters on the labia and vaginal opening
Pain during urination with some blood in the urine
explanation: Trichomoniasis typically causes a foul-smelling, frothy (often yellow-green) vaginal discharge. This is the most characteristic symptom.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Gastrointestinal Pancreatitis Clinical Presentation (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Patient suffers from pancreatitis with classic epigastric pain. Where would you see the pain refer? What would you find in the blood tests?
explanation: Classic pancreatitis pain radiates from the epigastrium to the back. Due to dehydration or acute kidney injury, blood tests often show elevated creatinine (and BUN).

topic: Reporting & Record-Keeping - Mandated Reporting Communicable Diseases (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Who are you required to report communicable disease to?
explanation: Healthcare providers must report certain communicable diseases to the local or state health department as mandated by law for public health surveillance and outbreak control.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Neurology Stroke Localization (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Naomi is a young 72 years old. ... Naomi has suffered a massive stroke of the left cerebral hemisphere (pons to be specific). Which of the following are the correct symptoms that would appear after such a stroke?
options: Right facial weakness, left body weakness
Right facial weakness and right body weakness
Left facial weakness and body weakness
Left facial weakness, right body weakness
correct: Right facial weakness and right body weakness
explanation: A left hemisphere stroke affects the right side of the body due to crossing of motor pathways. This causes right facial weakness (lower face) and right-sided hemiparesis (body weakness).

topic: Infection Control - HIV Transmission Modes (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Which of the following is NOT a mode of transmission for HIV?
explanation: HIV is transmitted through specific body fluids (blood, semen, vaginal secretions, breast milk). It is not transmitted through air or casual contact.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Infectious Diseases HIV Progression (Biomedical Sciences)
question: What is the average incubation period for HIV to AIDS?
explanation: Without treatment, the average time from HIV infection to the development of AIDS is approximately 8–10 years.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Cardiac Auscultation (Biomedical Sciences)
question: A patient with heart disease comes in to see his doctor. The doctor takes his stethoscope and places it at the junction of the 5th intercostal space and the mid-clavicular line. Which of the following sounds in the doctor listen to?
explanation: The 5th intercostal space at the mid-clavicular line (left side) is the standard location for auscultating the mitral valve (apex of the heart).

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Infectious Diseases EBV & Organomegaly (Biomedical Sciences)
question: While it’s never okay to needle into an organ, an acupuncturist must be extra careful not to needle into an enlarged liver or spleen in patients affected with this pathogen.
explanation: EBV (Epstein-Barr Virus) causes infectious mononucleosis, which frequently leads to splenomegaly (enlarged spleen) and sometimes hepatomegaly. Needling risk is high due to possible splenic rupture.

topic: Risk Management & Safety - CPR Adult Protocol (Biomedical Sciences)
question: You are performing adult CPR and have finished giving 30 compressions on the chest. What is the next thing to do?
options: Wait for a response before proceeding
Give the second round of 15 compressions
explanation: According to current adult CPR guidelines, after 30 chest compressions you should give 2 rescue breaths before continuing with the next set of compressions.

topic: Infection Control - Needle Safety & Sharps Handling (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Acupuncture needles should be handled carefully in order to prevent needle stick injuries. Which of the following methods is recommended in order to avoid injury?
options: Wear two pairs of latex gloves
Wear three pair of latex gloves
Wear one pair of latex gloves
explanation: The best way to prevent needle-stick injuries is proper handling technique, correct disposal into a sharps container, and following clean needle protocols. Multiple pairs of gloves are not recommended.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Endocrinology ADH Testing (Biomedical Sciences)
question: The ADH (Anti-diuretic hormone) blood test is performed on patients suspected of having:
explanation: ADH (vasopressin) regulates water balance. The test is primarily used to evaluate diabetes insipidus (a disorder of water regulation), where ADH levels or function are abnormal.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Endocrinology Hypothyroidism Causes (Biomedical Sciences)
question: What is the most common cause of hypothyroidism?
explanation: Hashimoto's thyroiditis is an autoimmune condition where the immune system attacks the thyroid gland. It is the leading cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions.

topic: Risk Management & Safety - CPR Initial Assessment (Biomedical Sciences)
question: What is the first step in CPR?
options: Determine if there are any body injuries
Determine if patient has a pulse
explanation: The first step in CPR is to check responsiveness (tap shoulder and shout “Are you okay?”) to confirm the person is unconscious before starting chest compressions.

topic: Infection Control - Clean Needle Technique (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Once an acupuncture point has been swabbed and the site prepared for acupuncture, which of the following is correct about touching the acupuncture point before needling?
options: Once swabbed, the acupuncture point can be touched but needs to be reswabbed after doing so.
Once swabbed, the acupuncture can not be touched.
Once swabbed, the acupuncture point can be touched.
Once swabbed, the acupuncture point can only be touched if the practitioner is wearing a latex glove.
correct: Once swabbed, the acupuncture point can be touched.
explanation: After proper hand cleaning and swabbing the point, the area is part of the clean field per CNT 7th edition. Palpation/touching of the swabbed point is allowed without reswabbing.

topic: Infection Control - PPE Glove Selection (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Which of the following materials should be avoided when purchasing gloves?
explanation: Latex gloves should be avoided due to the high risk of latex allergies in both practitioners and patients. Nitrile is the preferred alternative.

topic: Infection Control - Glove Use Indications (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Gloves should be worn in all but which of the following scenarios?
options: Potential exposure to blood or OPIM
explanation: Gloves are required when there is potential exposure to blood or OPIM (e.g., wet cupping, intra-oral palpation). Routine needle removal does not require gloves if proper clean technique is used and no blood is present.

topic: Infection Control - Glove Use for Specific Points (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Gloves are not generally required when performing acupuncture except when needling which of the following points?
explanation: Du27

topic: Infection Control - Post-Exposure Management (Biomedical Sciences)
question: If you experience a needle stick or sharps injury or are exposed to the blood or OPIM of a patient, all the following steps should be followed with the exception of which one?
options: Flush splashes to the nose, mouth, or skin with water.
Seek medical advice from a licensed physician as soon as possible.
Wash needle stick locations and cuts with soap and water.
Irrigate eyes with clean water, saline, or mouthwash.
correct: Irrigate eyes with clean water, saline, or mouthwash.
explanation: For eye exposure, irrigate immediately with clean water or saline only. Mouthwash is not appropriate for the eyes.

topic: Infection Control - Hand Hygiene Drying Technique (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Which of the following methods is most effective to use when drying hands after washing?
explanation: Gently patting hands dry with a clean paper towel is the recommended method. Rubbing can cause skin irritation and micro-tears that increase infection risk.

topic: Infection Control - Post-Exposure Evaluation Timeline (Biomedical Sciences)
question: In some states it is recommended that someone with a needle stick injury be evaluated within which of the following periods of time after such an incident takes place?
explanation: Needle-stick injuries should be evaluated as soon as possible. Many state guidelines and protocols recommend medical evaluation within 2 hours for best effectiveness of post-exposure prophylaxis.

topic: Infection Control - Healthcare Worker Screening (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Which of the following tests is recommended for acupuncturists to have annually?
explanation: TST (Tuberculin Skin Test) is recommended annually for healthcare workers, including acupuncturists, to screen for tuberculosis (TB) exposure.

topic: Infection Control - Hand Hygiene Indications (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Hands should be washed in all but which of the following situations?
options: Before locking up the clinic at the end of the day
correct: Before locking up the clinic at the end of the day
explanation: Per CNT 7th ed., handwashing is required after patient contact, after eating, after phone use, etc. However, if no new contamination occurs after the last patient, there is no need to wash hands again just before locking up the clinic at the end of the day.

topic: Infection Control - Hand Hygiene Water Temperature (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Which of the following water temperatures should be avoided when washing hands?
explanation: Hot water should be avoided because it can damage the skin, leading to dryness and cracks that increase infection risk. Warm water is preferred.

topic: Infection Control - Glove Change Indications (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Gloves should be removed or changed for a new pair in all of the following scenarios, except for which of the following?
options: After needling a point near mucous membranes before needling the next point on a mucous membrane
After contact with medical equipment or room surfaces
correct: After needling a point near mucous membranes before needling the next point on a mucous membrane
explanation: Gloves must be changed after patient contact, between patients, and after touching contaminated surfaces/equipment. Changing is not required when moving between mucous membrane points if no blood or contamination occurs.

topic: Infection Control - Lab Coat Usage (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Which of the following statements is not true about the use of lab coats?
options: Lab coats can be used when performing acupuncture.
Lab coats are personal protective equipment and should be worn in the lab when working with chemicals and biologicals to protect the skin and clothing from splatter and spills.
Do not wear lab coats in public places, such as offices, lunchrooms, lounge areas, or elsewhere.
Sleeves on a lab coat can be rolled up when performing acupuncture.
correct: Sleeves on a lab coat can be rolled up when performing acupuncture.
explanation: Sleeves should NOT be rolled up during acupuncture or clinical procedures. Rolled sleeves compromise the protective barrier of the lab coat.

topic: Infection Control - PPE Removal Sequence (Biomedical Sciences)
question: You are performing wet cupping and notice that there is a tear in your gloves. All of the following steps should be performed, with the exception of which one?
options: Avoid spreading contamination by limiting surfaces and items touched with contaminated gloves.
Remove your goggles or lab coat before removing contaminated gloves.
Remove gloves immediate if they are torn or contaminated.
Wash hands before putting on another pair of gloves.
correct: Remove your goggles or lab coat before removing contaminated gloves.
explanation: When gloves are torn or contaminated, remove the gloves first before removing other PPE (goggles/lab coat). Removing other items first can spread contamination.

topic: Infection Control - Skin Flora & Hand Hygiene (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Which of the following areas of the skin is most heavily colonized by gram-negative bacilli such as E. cloacae, Klebsiella, and Acinetobacter?
explanation: The subungual area (under the fingernails) is moist and protected, making it the most heavily colonized by gram-negative bacteria such as E. cloacae, Klebsiella, and Acinetobacter.

topic: Infection Control - Hand Hygiene Preparation (Biomedical Sciences)
question: When preparing to wash your hands, which of the following steps should be performed first?
options: Place paper towels next to the sink
Place the bar of soap near the sink
Turn on the water and adjust the temperature
explanation: Remove jewelry (rings, watches, bracelets) first because it can harbor germs and interfere with thorough handwashing.

topic: Infection Control - Hand Hygiene Purpose (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Handwashing is aimed at reducing or eliminating which of the following substances from the hand?
explanation: Handwashing primarily reduces transient (temporary) skin flora picked up from the environment or patients. Resident flora lives deeper and is not fully removed by routine washing.

topic: Infection Control - Bleeding Risk Areas (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Which of the following types of acupuncture increases the chance of bleeding?
explanation: The scalp has a rich blood supply and thin skin, which increases the chance of bleeding during acupuncture.

topic: Infection Control - Responsibility for PPE Policies (Biomedical Sciences)
question: In an acupuncture clinic with front desk staff, acupuncture assistants, interns and/or more than one licensed acupuncturist, which of the following workers decides when gloves should be worn?
explanation: Per OSHA BBP Standard and CNT Manual 7th ed. p.182, the employer (clinic owner) must establish policies on glove use. Individual employees follow the employer's policies. Self-employed practitioners must create their own guidelines.

topic: Infection Control - Skin Disinfectants (Biomedical Sciences)
question: A disinfecting solution containing chlorhexidine gluconate can be used to clean the patient’s skin. Which of the following is not a brand name for chlorhexidine?
explanation: Hibistat, Spectrum-4, and Calgone Vesta are brand names containing chlorhexidine gluconate. Sporox is a hydrogen peroxide/peracetic acid product, not chlorhexidine.

topic: Infection Control - Skin Preparation (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Iodine can be used to clean a patient’s skin prior to acupuncture treatment under which of the following circumstances?
options: Iodine should be used to clear a patient's skin after needling if they have excessive bleeding.
Iodine should never be used to clean a patient's skin prior to needling.
Iodine can be used to clean a patient's skin after needling.
Iodine should be used to clear a patient's skin prior to needling.
correct: Iodine should never be used to clean a patient's skin prior to needling.
explanation: Iodine is generally not recommended for routine skin prep before needling due to potential skin irritation. Alcohol is the preferred agent.

topic: Infection Control - Clinic Attire (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Which of the following pieces of clothing is acceptable for an acupuncturist to wear in the clinic?
explanation: Close-toed shoes are the only safe and appropriate footwear option in the clinic. Open-toed shoes, loose long hair, and certain skirts/dresses increase risk of injury or contamination.

topic: Infection Control - Hand Hygiene Alternatives (Biomedical Sciences)
question: If the practitioner’s hands are soiled and no soap and running water are available, which of the following substances can be used as an alternative?
explanation: When hands are visibly soiled and soap + water are unavailable, antimicrobial-impregnated wipes (towelettes) are an acceptable alternative. Alcohol products are not suitable for visibly dirty hands.

topic: Infection Control - Eye Protection (Biomedical Sciences)
question: When there is a risk of blood or OPIM exposure, which of the following circumstances would make contact lenses a more suitable alternative to goggles?
options: Only if the person has a stigmatism.
Only if the person is near-sighted.
Only if the person is far-sighted.
explanation: Contact lenses are never an acceptable substitute for goggles when there is risk of blood or OPIM splash. Goggles provide necessary splash protection to the eyes.

topic: Infection Control - Hand Drying Methods (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Which of the following methods of hand drying minimizes the spread of contaminants after hand washing?
explanation: Single-use paper towels minimize the spread of germs because they are discarded after one use. Shared cloth or roll towels can harbor bacteria.

topic: Infection Control - Needle Stick Prevention (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding prevention of needle stick injuries?
options: Gloves always protect the practitioner from needle stick injuries.
Gloves do not protect against needle stick injuries.
Gloves protect patients from needle stick injuries.
Gloves only protect the practitioners from needle stick injuries some of the time.
correct: Gloves do not protect against needle stick injuries.
explanation: Gloves help prevent blood/fluid exposure but do NOT protect against needle sticks. Needles can easily penetrate gloves. Safe handling and disposal are key.

topic: Infection Control - Handwashing Effectiveness (Biomedical Sciences)
question: Handwashing with plain soap and water has which of the following results?
options: Increases the transmission of healthcare associated infections (HAI).
Decreases the transmission of healthcare-associated infections (HAI).
Provides a false sense of security to practitioners.
Creates a barrier between the skin and contaminants.
correct: Decreases the transmission of healthcare-associated infections (HAI).
explanation: Handwashing with plain soap and water physically removes dirt and germs, which significantly reduces the spread of healthcare-associated infections.

topic: Infection Control - Handwashing Duration
question: Which of the following lengths of time is required for scrubbing your hands with soap before rinsing them off?
explanation: According to standard healthcare and CDC guidelines, practitioners should scrub their hands with soap for at least 15 to 20 seconds to effectively remove pathogens before rinsing.

topic: Infection Control - Hand Sanitizer Use
question: When using hand sanitizer, practitioners should rub the product over all surfaces of their hands and fingers and follow which of the following protocols?
explanation: According to CDC and healthcare infection control guidelines, hand sanitizer must be rubbed thoroughly over all surfaces of the hands until they are completely dry to ensure pathogens are effectively destroyed.

topic: Infection Control - Bloodborne Pathogen Risk
question: Which of the following bloodborne pathogens is most likely to be passed to the practitioner by needlestick exposure?
explanation: Hepatitis B (HBV) has the highest rate of transmission after a needlestick injury, with a risk of up to 30% in unvaccinated individuals. In comparison, Hepatitis C (HCV) is around 1.8%, and HIV is approximately 0.3%. Hepatitis A (HAV) is transmitted via the fecal-oral route, not typically through bloodborne exposure.

topic: Infection Control - Handwashing Rinse Technique
question: When washing your hands before a treatment, practitioners should scrub their hands for 10-15 seconds. The next step is to rinse their hands well under clean, running water with their hands ________________.
explanation: During the rinsing phase of handwashing, hands should be held lower than the elbows so that the water flows from the least contaminated area (the wrists) to the most contaminated area (the fingertips), preventing dirty water from running up the forearms.

topic: Infection Control - Clean Field Maintenance
question: Which of the following items should not be placed on a clean field?
options: Guide tube that has been used to insert a needle into a point on the same patient
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual (7th ed.), a jar of cotton balls or a jar of unopened swabs cannot be placed on the clean field because the container itself is not sterile or properly sanitized. Conversely, a clean, previously-sterilized guide tube may be handled and replaced back onto the clean field for multiple insertions on the same patient.

topic: Infection Control - Technique Level Classification
question: Acupuncture is considered to have which of the following levels of infection control?
explanation: Acupuncture is classified as a clean technique (hence 'Clean Needle Technique'). While the needles themselves must be sterile, the clinical environment, practitioner hands, and patient skin are prepared to a 'clean' standard to significantly minimize infection risk rather than maintaining a completely sterile field.

topic: Infection Control - Needle Insertion into Guide Tube
question: The CNT Manual strongly recommends that when inserting a needle into the guide tube, the needle is inserted in which of the following ways?
options: You should only use needles with guide tubes attached.
While the needle is in the package
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual, if a needle is inserted into a separate guide tube, it must be inserted handle first to avoid bending, damaging, or contaminating the sterile needle tip.

topic: Infection Control - Exposure to Non-Intact Skin
question: In the event that non-intact skin is exposed to blood or body fluids, it is recommended that the hands be cleaned with which of the following substances, followed by the use of a single-use paper towel to dry them?
options: Hand sanitizer first and then soap and water
explanation: According to healthcare infection control standards and the CNT manual, if non-intact skin is exposed to blood or body fluids, the area must be washed immediately and thoroughly with soap and water to mechanically remove and destroy pathogens. Harsh chemicals or sanitizers alone are not recommended for open skin exposure.

topic: Infection Control - Sharps Disposal Protocol
question: After withdrawing a needle, which of the following protocols should be carried out?
options: Placed on the clean field on the treatment table
Placed in a tray; once all have been removed, dispose of them in the sharps container
Immediately placed in the sharps container
Handed to your assistant, who will place it in the sharps container
correct: Immediately placed in the sharps container
explanation: According to OSHA and Clean Needle Technique (CNT) standards, used needles must be disposed of immediately into a sharps container upon removal from the patient to minimize the risk of accidental needlestick injuries. They should never be placed on an intermediate surface or passed to another person.

topic: Infection Control - Hand Hygiene Requirements
question: Hand washing with soap and water is not strictly required in which of the following scenarios if an alcohol-based hand sanitizer is used instead?
options: Before and after eating, after using the restroom or after sneezing or coughing
Upon entering and before inserting acupuncture needles or performing other clinical procedures
explanation: While hand hygiene must always be performed before donning gloves, CDC and CNT guidelines permit the use of an alcohol-based hand sanitizer instead of full soap-and-water hand washing for this step, provided the hands are not visibly soiled. Full washing is mandatory after restroom use or eating.

topic: Risk Management - Safe Needling Depth (Ren 12)
question: According to the CNT Manual, which of the following depths are safest when needling a thin patient at Ren 12 (Zhongwan)?
explanation: To prevent accidental penetration of the peritoneal cavity or internal organs in thin patients, the CNT manual notes that a safe limit for absolute physical depth on the upper abdomen is 0.5 inch. Safety guidelines generally quantify tissue depth limits in absolute imperial or metric measurements rather than proportional cun.

topic: Infection Control - Recommended vs Essential Practices
question: Which of the following CNT protocols is recommended but not essential?
options: Swabbing the patient’s skin with alcohol prior to acupuncture
Wearing gloves when there is the potential for exposure to OPIM
Using a new guide tube with each patient
correct: Swabbing the patient’s skin with alcohol prior to acupuncture
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual, swabbing skin with alcohol is a recommended practice but not an essential/mandatory step for routine acupuncture if the skin is already visibly clean. Hand hygiene, using fresh guide tubes per patient, and wearing gloves for potential OPIM exposure are strictly essential.

topic: Infection Control - Point Palpation Protocol
question: An acupuncturist can palpate the point to be needled after carrying out which of the following actions?
options: Once their hands are cleaned and after the point has been swabbed
Once their hands are cleaned and before the point has been swabbed only
Once their hands are cleaned, either before or after the insertion point is swabbed
Before washing their hands, after the point has been swabbed
correct: Once their hands are cleaned and after the point has been swabbed
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual (7th ed.), it is acceptable clean technique to palpate the acupuncture point after cleaning the skin, provided the hands are clean. After this cleaning of the hands, nothing should be touched except the needle handle, guide tube, and the skin over the point.

topic: Infection Control - Skin Preparation Protocol
question: Which of the following protocols is correct?
options: Place the sharps container on the clean field
Swab the first point and immediately insert the needle
Swab the patient’s skin and wait for the alcohol to dry before needling
Place the alcohol dispenser on the clean field
correct: Swab the patient’s skin and wait for the alcohol to dry before needling
explanation: According to the CNT Manual, practitioners must allow alcohol to dry completely on the skin before inserting a needle. This maximizes the antiseptic effect of the alcohol and prevents the patient from experiencing unnecessary pain or stinging. Heavy equipment like containers and dispensers must never be placed on the clean field.

topic: Infection Control - Sterilized Items Placement
question: In which of the following areas should sterilized items be placed on the clean field?
options: Near the clean field but not on it
In a tray on the clean field but not on the clean field itself
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual, sterilized items (such as sterile needles and sterile cotton balls/gauze) must be placed in the center of the clean field. Non-sterilized but clean items, such as sealed alcohol swabs, are placed on the periphery or edges of the clean field.

topic: Risk Management - Components of CNT
question: There are seven components of Clean Needle Technique. Hand sanitation, establishing and maintaining a clean field, skin preparation, standard precautions, and isolation of contaminated sharps are part of this list. Which of the following options is also one of the core components?
options: Renewing the Clean Needle Technique certificate every two years
Following emergency protocols for needlestick and other accidents
correct: Following emergency protocols for needlestick and other accidents
explanation: The core components of Clean Needle Technique include hand hygiene, establishing a clean field, skin preparation, needle handling, isolation of sharps, standard precautions, and following emergency protocols for needlestick injuries and other clinical accidents.

topic: Infection Control - Hand Sanitizer Specifications
question: Soap and water are the best ways to reduce the number of microbes. When soap and water are not available, which of the following products is most effective?
options: Alcohol based hand sanitizer containing at least 70% alcohol
Alcohol based hand sanitizer containing at least 60% alcohol
correct: Alcohol based hand sanitizer containing at least 60% alcohol
explanation: According to the CDC and healthcare infection control guidelines, when soap and water are unavailable, an alcohol-based hand sanitizer containing at least 60% alcohol should be used to effectively reduce the number of viable microbes on the hands.

topic: Infection Control - Missed Point Re-needling
question: You are needling the extra point Dingchuan. You miss the point and need to re-needle the point. Which of the following methods is safest?
options: Use the same needle but on the other side of the body
Dispose of the needle in the sharps container and use a new needle
Re-using the needle or using a new one are both recommended
correct: Dispose of the needle in the sharps container and use a new needle
explanation: According to Clean Needle Technique (CNT) safety guidelines, once a needle has been inserted into a patient's skin, it is considered contaminated. If a practitioner misses the point and needs to re-needle, that needle must be discarded immediately into the sharps container, and a new sterile needle must be used to prevent cross-contamination or transferring deep tissue pathogens.

topic: Infection Control - Maintaining Hand Hygiene Transit
question: You have washed your hands and are returning to the treatment room. Between you and the treatment room are two doors. You should open the doors in which of the following ways?
options: Turn the door handles wearing a disposable glove
Leave the doors between the bathroom and the treatment rooms open
Turn the door handles with a paper towel
Turn the door handles with your clean hands
correct: Turn the door handles with a paper towel
explanation: According to standard healthcare and Clean Needle Technique (CNT) protocols, to maintain hand hygiene after washing, a practitioner must avoid touching contaminated surfaces like door handles. Using a clean paper towel as a barrier ensures hands remain clean while transitioning back into the treatment room.

topic: Infection Control - Long Needle Insertion Technique
question: When using a long needle (3 – 6 inches), which of the following techniques is used to support the needle shaft during insertion?
options: With cotton or gauze between the fingers and the needle shaft
With sterile cotton between the fingers and needle shaft
correct: With sterile cotton between the fingers and needle shaft
explanation: According to Clean Needle Technique (CNT) criteria, if a long needle requires shaft support during insertion to prevent bending, the practitioner must use a sterile barrier (such as a sterile cotton ball or sterile gauze) between their fingers and the needle shaft to maintain absolute sterility. Non-sterile cotton or bare fingers are strict violations.

topic: Infection Control - Re-contamination of Hands
question: You are getting ready to needle your patient. You have washed your hands. The clean field is prepared. The skin is swabbed with alcohol and the alcohol has dried. As you go to insert your first needle, your hair falls in front of your eyes. You push the hair behind your ear and then take which of the following actions?
options: Tie your hair back in a ponytail
Palpate the patient’s skin before inserting the needle
Insert the needle into the first point
explanation: According to the CNT Manual, if a practitioner touches a contaminated surface—including their own hair, face, skin, or clothing—after performing hand hygiene, their hands are considered contaminated. The practitioner must re-clean their hands using soap and water or an alcohol-based hand sanitizer before proceeding with the treatment.

topic: Infection Control - Sharps Container Management
question: Sharps containers are placed in which of the following areas of the treatment room, and replaced when they are at which of the following levels?
options: On the wall near the treatment table; one-third
explanation: According to OSHA and Clean Needle Technique (CNT) standards, sharps containers must be located as close as practical to the area where sharps are used (such as beside the treatment table) and must be replaced or sealed when they reach three-quarters (75%) full to prevent overfilling and accidental needlestick injuries.

topic: Infection Control - Swab and Cotton Ball Reuse
question: A new and clean swab/cotton ball is required in which of the following scenarios?
options: Whenever the swab/cotton ball is visibly dirty/contaminated/too dry/each patient
correct: Whenever the swab/cotton ball is visibly dirty/contaminated/too dry/each patient
explanation: According to the CNT Manual, a single alcohol swab can be used to clean multiple acupuncture points on the same patient if the skin is non-soiled. However, a new swab is strictly required if the current one becomes visibly dirty, contaminated, dried out, or when switching to a different patient.

topic: Infection Control - Glove Use Indications
question: In which of the following scenarios are gloves not worn?
options: When there is or might be bleeding or OPIM
When needling the genitals or mouth or palpating near skin lesions
If the practitioner has open wounds or skin lesions on the acupuncturist’s hand
explanation: According to the CNT Manual and universal precautions, gloves are not routinely required for palpating intact skin, such as a standard abdominal examination. Gloves are strictly mandatory when handling blood/OPIM, needling mucous membranes, or when either the practitioner or patient has non-intact skin or lesions.

topic: Infection Control - Unused Open Needle Disposal
question: You open three blister packs of needles for a treatment and only use two of the three packs of needles. You have another patient arriving in 15 minutes. Which of the following actions is most appropriate to take with the already opened third pack of needles?
options: Dispose of it in the trash
Use it for your next patient
Reseal and use it another day
Dispose of it in the sharps container
correct: Dispose of it in the sharps container
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual (7th ed.), when using acupuncture needles from multi-packs, all needles left over at the end of a treatment must be treated as non-sterile sharps. They cannot be saved for later use or used on another patient, and they must be discarded in an appropriate sharps container to prevent accidental puncture injuries.

topic: Infection Control - Table Surface Disinfection
question: The work surface used for the clean field should be cleaned at least once daily using which of the following types of cleaners?
explanation: According to the CNT Manual, environmental surfaces such as the treatment table or workspace used to set up a clean field must be cleaned at least once daily (or when visibly soiled) using an EPA-registered low-level disinfectant or a 1:100 bleach solution. High-level disinfectants and liquid sterilants like glutaraldehyde are reserved for semi-critical instruments, not environmental surfaces.

topic: Infection Control - Clean Field Materials
question: Which of the following is considered an inappropriate item to use as a clean field?
options: Metal tray with a paper barrier
explanation: According to the CNT Manual, a clean field must consist of a clean, disposable barrier (such as a fresh paper towel or table paper) or a sanitized tray with a barrier liner. The bare treatment table itself is an environmental surface exposed to patients and contaminants, making it completely inappropriate to use as a clean field without a barrier.

topic: Infection Control - Sterility Requirement for Skin-Piercing Objects
question: Any object that pierces the skin must have which of the following qualities?
explanation: According to health regulations and Clean Needle Technique (CNT) standards, any medical instrument or object that penetrates the skin barrier must be completely sterile to eliminate the risk of introducing pathogens directly into deep tissues or the bloodstream. Clean or disinfected objects may still harbor highly resilient bacterial spores.

topic: Infection Control - Needle Withdrawal Site Care
question: After removing the acupuncture needle, cover the hole by using which of the following methods?
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual, after withdrawing an acupuncture needle, the practitioner should apply pressure to the insertion site using a clean, dry cotton ball or gauze pad if bleeding or fluid release occurs. A wet cotton ball (e.g., with alcohol) will sting and inhibit clotting, while bare hands or fingers pose a cross-contamination and bloodborne pathogen risk.

topic: Infection Control - Bloodborne Pathogen Transmission Risk
question: Which of the following risk factors is most likely for the transmission of bloodborne pathogens in a clinical setting?
options: Not replacing sharps containers on a regular basis
Not using high level disinfectants to wipe down surfaces
explanation: In an acupuncture or clinical setting, accidental needlestick injuries (percutaneous exposure) represent the primary and most high-probability route for transmitting bloodborne pathogens such as HBV, HCV, and HIV. While other safety failures increase risk, a sharps puncture provides direct bloodstream access for contaminated fluids.

topic: Infection Control - Cross Infection Risk Factors
question: Which of the following will increase the risk of cross-infection?
explanation: According to Clean Needle Technique (CNT) protocols, utilizing a wet cotton ball or swab on a fresh insertion site can facilitate the transport of surface microbes into the puncture wound via capillary action, increasing the risk of cross-infection. It also inhibits normal platelet coagulation and causes patient discomfort.

topic: Infection Control - Japanese Meridian Therapy Oshide Technique
question: When performing contact needling, the needle is placed between which of the following two fingers while resting them on the skin at the acupuncture point?
options: Between the clean thumb and index finger of the non-dominant hand
Between the clean thumb and index finger of the dominant hand
Between the clean thumb and middle finger of the dominant hand
Between the clean thumb and middle finger of the non-dominant hand
correct: Between the clean thumb and index finger of the non-dominant hand
explanation: In Japanese acupuncture (meridian therapy), the non-dominant hand is known as the 'oshide' (pressing hand). During contact needling or insertion, the needle is stabilized and guided between the tips of the clean thumb and index finger of this non-dominant hand while resting on the skin. Because these fingers directly touch the skin near the insertion site, they must be thoroughly clean to avoid cross-contamination.

topic: Infection Control - Toyohari Post-Needle Skin Contact
question: When performing Toyohari acupuncture, after the needle removal, the skin comes in contact with which of the following items on the spot where the needle had been in contact with the skin?
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual, Toyohari acupuncture primarily utilizes non-insertive contact needling where the needle does not penetrate the skin barrier. Because there is no puncture and zero risk of blood or OPIM being present, it is an acceptable variation for the practitioner to place a clean finger directly on the spot immediately after removing the needle.

topic: Infection Control - Travel Kit Supply Packaging
question: When preparing a travel kit, which of the following items is not placed in its own smaller ziplock plastic bag?
explanation: According to Clean Needle Technique (CNT) travel kit guidelines, items such as cotton balls, gloves, and clean fields must be grouped and sealed in individual plastic bags to maintain cleanliness. Individually wrapped commercial items, such as alcohol prep pads, are already factory-sealed and do not require additional individual bagging.

topic: Federal Regulations - Regulated Biohazard Waste Thresholds
question: OSHA defines cotton balls soaked with blood that can be wrung out as being medical waste. If there is less blood than that, the cotton ball should be placed in which of the following containers?
explanation: According to OSHA standards and Clean Needle Technique (CNT) protocols, personal protective equipment or clinical items (like cotton balls or gauze) contaminated with blood are only considered regulated biohazard waste if they are saturated to the point of releasing fluid when compressed. Items with minor, non-saturated blood spots are classified as regular solid waste and should be disposed of in a standard trash receptacle.

topic: Federal Regulations - Alternative Sharps Container Labeling
question: In all states, use of a commercially prepared sharps container will meet the regulations for sharps disposal. If a non-commercial container is legal for use (such as a pill bottle with a screw-on cap), be sure to mark the container with which of the following labels?
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual (7th ed.), if an alternative, non-commercial sharps container is legally permitted for use, it must be clearly marked with the biohazard symbol. This ensures all clinical staff and sanitation workers recognize that the container holds hazardous medical waste, requiring disposal according to biohazardous waste laws.

topic: Infection Control - Acupuncture Travel Kit Organization
question: When creating a travel kit, which of the following two items are not kept in bags?
options: 2 x 2 gauze pads and alcohol prep pads
explanation: According to standard Clean Needle Technique (CNT) travel kit parameters, clean tools and medical supplies must be separated into structured gallon-sized bags. However, the manual dictates that the hemostat (or tweezers) and the alcohol-based hand sanitizer are explicitly classified as items not kept inside individual bags within the travel carrier for immediate accessibility and hygiene sequencing.

topic: Infection Control - Hand Hygiene for Off-Site Treatments
question: You are on a house call. It is the end of the treatment. When is it required that the practitioner washes his/her/their hands?
options: Immediately after removing needles before handling anything else only
Immediately after removing the needles and again after packing up the equipment
Before packing up the equipment only
correct: Immediately after removing the needles and again after packing up the equipment
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual guidelines for travel kits and off-site treatments, hand hygiene must be performed immediately after withdrawing the final needle before handling any clean travel kit bags. It must be performed a second time after all equipment has been packed up to ensure the practitioner is sanitized before departure.

topic: Infection Control - Travel Kit Material Layout Sequence
question: When setting out the materials from the travel kit during a house call, the CNT Manual recommends which of the following items be placed last, outside the clean field?
options: Blister pack of needles in the original packaging
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual guidelines for travel kits, the clean field and all clean/sterile materials (needles, cotton balls, tweezers) must be laid out first. The non-clean items, specifically the waste bag and the sharps container, are removed from the kit and set up last, completely outside the perimeter of the clean field to prevent cross-contamination.

topic: Infection Control - Soap and Water vs Sanitizer Indications
question: Handwashing is one of the most problematic topics within a public health or group treatment setting. Practitioner’s hands should be washed with soap and water in all but which of the following scenarios?
options: On arrival and before leaving work
Before eating and after restroom use
When hands are dirty with some organic matter, such as blood
explanation: According to the CDC and the CCAOM CNT Manual, alcohol-based hand sanitizer is acceptable and often preferred for routine hand hygiene between patients if the hands are not visibly soiled. Handwashing with physical soap and water is strictly mandatory upon arriving/leaving the clinic, before eating, after restroom use, or when hands are contaminated with blood or organic matter.

topic: Risk Management - Upright Patient Positioning Safety
question: When positioning a patient sitting up, it is essential to ensure all but which of the following considerations are taken?
options: Encourage the patient to use the bathroom prior to treatment
Legs and arms are not crossed
The patient is comfortable and the patient’s head is supported
The patient is offered a blanket during treatment
correct: The patient is offered a blanket during treatment
explanation: According to standard clinical safety protocols and the CNT Manual, essential positioning requirements for a sitting patient focus on safety and stability (supporting the head to prevent fainting injury, uncrossing limbs to prevent muscle tension/needle distortion, and emptying the bladder to avoid movement). While offering a blanket is excellent for general patient comfort, it is not a strict positioning safety requirement.

topic: Infection Control - Community Acupuncture Setting Barriers
question: Treatment chairs in community acupuncture clinic settings should be cleaned between patients and covered with which of the following materials?
explanation: According to Clean Needle Technique (CNT) guidelines for community or group acupuncture settings, all treatment chair surfaces must be disinfected between patient visits. To maintain a hygienic barrier, chairs should be covered with disposable table paper or a fresh sheet for each patient. Porous cloth materials like blankets or quilts cannot be properly sanitized between consecutive appointments and increase cross-contamination risks.

topic: Infection Control - Hand Washing Sequence for Travel Kit Assembly
question: Acupuncture travel kits should be prepared in a way that all items remain clean. The hard-sided container must be washed inside and out with soapy water and dried with paper towels. Ziploc bags should be fresh from the package and free of rips and holes. Which of the following times is it required for the practitioner to wash their hands?
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual (7th ed., p. 86), after preparing the hard-sided container and gathering fresh plastic bags, the practitioner must wash their hands explicitly before assembling the kit. This step ensures that no skin oils, dust, or contaminants are transferred onto the fresh Ziploc bags, paper towels, cotton balls, or needle boxes as they are packed inside the mobile carrier.

topic: Infection Control - Portable Waste Disposal in Travel Kits
question: When preparing a travel kit, which of the following items can serve as a portable trash can?
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual guidelines for travel kits, a plastic-lined paper waste bag should be included to serve as a portable trash receptacle for non-sharp waste. The paper design allows the bag to stand upright independently outside the clean field, while the plastic lining ensures that moisture or trace bodily fluids do not seep through.

topic: Infection Control - Clean Field Handling and Unfolding Techniques
question: To preserve the cleanliness of the clean field, the practitioner is strongly recommended to handle the clean field in which of the following ways in order not to contaminate the center of the field?
explanation: According to Clean Needle Technique (CNT) protocols, when establishing a clean field using a paper towel or commercially prepared drape, the practitioner should handle the material strictly by its four corners or outer edges. This practice ensures that the central working surface—where sterile needles and clean instruments will be placed—remains completely uncontaminated by the practitioner's hands.

topic: Infection Control - Toyohari Needle Shaft Handling Rules
question: When performing Toyohari acupuncture, the standards of handwashing, setting up a clean field, immediately isolating used sharps, and following Standard Precautions remain the same as with all acupuncture needling techniques. Which of the following variations apply to the contact of the shaft of the needle in this style?
options: May be touched by the practitioner’s fingers when treating patients with strong immune systems
May not be touched by the practitioner’s fingers
May be touched by the practitioner’s fingers if the practitioner wears gloves
May be touched by the practitioner’s fingers
correct: May be touched by the practitioner’s fingers
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual, Toyohari acupuncture is a non-insertive style where the needle rests on the skin without breaking the epidermis. Because there is no penetration and no entry pathway for infection into deeper tissues, the shaft of the needle may be touched by the practitioner's clean fingers to facilitate the technique.

topic: Infection Control - Mid-Treatment Interruption and Needle Reuse Laws
question: During a community acupuncture treatment, the patient needs to go to the restroom. You remove the needles. The patient goes to the bathroom and returns to the treatment area. You insert which of the following needles into the patient when resuming the treatment?
options: Same needles if they were not inserted too deeply
explanation: According to Clean Needle Technique (CNT) strict infection control protocols and federal safety guidelines, once an acupuncture needle is withdrawn from the body, it is classified as used hazardous waste and cannot be reinserted under any circumstances. If a treatment is interrupted (such as a restroom break), completely new, sterile, single-use needles must be utilized to resume care to prevent cross-contamination.

topic: Infection Control - Travel Kit Isolation of Non-Clean Items
question: Which non-clean item is placed inside its own gallon-sized ziplock plastic bag?
options: A smaller paper bag with a plastic liner to receive trash
correct: A smaller paper bag with a plastic liner to receive trash
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual guidelines for travel kits, non-clean items must be isolated from clean materials. The smaller plastic-lined paper waste bag used to receive trash is explicitly classified as a non-clean item that must be packed inside its own dedicated gallon-sized Ziploc bag within the kit to prevent cross-contamination.

topic: Infection Control - Permissible Travel Kit Containers
question: Which of the following travel kits is most appropriate?
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual, an acupuncture travel kit must be housed in a hard-sided, rigid container that can be thoroughly washed inside and out with hot, soapy water and dried. Porous materials like canvas or leather cannot be adequately sanitized, and soft plastic bags offer no structural protection. A hard-sided make up box perfectly meets these strict hygiene and structural requirements.

topic: Infection Control - Hepatitis D Incubation Period Guidelines
question: According to the CNT manual, which of the following incubation periods corresponds to Hepatitis D (HDV)?
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual, the incubation period for Hepatitis D (HDV) is classified as unknown. Because HDV is a defective RNA virus that requires the concomitant presence of the Hepatitis B virus (HBV) to replicate, its timeline varies widely depending on whether it is acquired as a co-infection or a super-infection.

topic: Infection Control - Hepatitis B Vaccine Immunity Duration
question: After receiving the Hepatitis B vaccines, which of the following time periods represents how long immunity lasts?
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual and CDC guidelines, the series of Hepatitis B vaccines provides long-term protection, with immunologic memory remaining intact and effective for at least 20 years. Booster doses are not routinely recommended for healthy individuals who have completed the vaccine series.

topic: Infection Control - Hepatitis B Transmission Routes
question: Which of the following behaviors does not lead to HBV transmission?
explanation: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is transmitted through exposure to infective blood, semen, and other body fluids. It can be spread through contaminated needles, unprotected sexual intercourse, or sharing personal care items like razors or toothbrushes that cause micro-trauma and blood exchange. Casual contact and non-contaminated fomites, such as sharing dry clothing, do not transmit HBV.

topic: Infection Control - Hepatitis D Virology Nomenclature
question: Which of the following names is also used for Hepatitis D?
explanation: Hepatitis D (HDV) is commonly referred to in clinical virology as the Delta virus or delta hepatitis. It is a defective RNA satellite virus that can only propagate in the presence of the Hepatitis B virus (HBV), and its primary structural marker is historically classified as the delta antigen.

topic: Pharmacology - Herb-Drug Interactions and Interferon Safety
question: Which of the following herbs and formulas should not be prescribed to patients taking Interferon, a pharmaceutical drug used to treat HEP C (HCV)?
options: Huang Qi (Astragali Radix); Bu Zhong Yi Qi Tang (Tonify the Middle to Augment the Qi Decoction)
Chuan Xiong (Chuanxiong Rhizoma); Si Wu Tang (Four Substance Decoction)
Chai Hu (Bupleuri Radix); Xiao Chai Hu Tang (Minor Bupleurum Decoction)
Ren Shen (Ginseng Radix); Si Jun Zi Tang (Four Gentlemen Decoction)
correct: Chai Hu (Bupleuri Radix); Xiao Chai Hu Tang (Minor Bupleurum Decoction)
explanation: Clinical safety data confirms that concurrent administration of Chai Hu (Bupleuri Radix) or the formula Xiao Chai Hu Tang (Sho-saiko-to) with pharmaceutical Interferon therapies is strictly contraindicated. Combining these agents significantly escalates the risk of a patient developing drug-induced interstitial pneumonia, a severe and potentially fatal acute pulmonary inflammation driven by hyperactivated immune cytokine cascades in lung tissue.

topic: Infection Control - Hepatitis C Risk Factors and Transmission Efficiency
question: Which of the following is not considered a “serious risk” that increases the chances of contracting HCV?
options: Sexual contact with the same partner
correct: Sexual contact with the same partner
explanation: According to the CDC and the CCAOM CNT Manual, Hepatitis C (HCV) is primarily a bloodborne pathogen transmitted via percutaneous blood exposure, making needle sharing the highest risk factor. Co-infections like HIV and concurrent STDs severely escalate transmission risk due to mucosal breaks and immune compromise. In contrast, routine sexual contact within a long-term, stable, monogamous relationship is classified as a negligible or minimal risk vector, rather than a serious risk.

topic: Infection Control - Fecal-Oral Hepatitis Transmission Dynamics
question: Which of the following Hepatitis virus strains spreads by poor sanitation and personal hygiene?
explanation: According to public health standards and the CCAOM CNT Manual, Hepatitis A (HAV) is transmitted via the fecal-oral route, which is heavily facilitated by poor community sanitation, contaminated water or food supplies, and inadequate personal hand hygiene. In contrast, HBV, HCV, and HDV are strictly bloodborne pathogens transmitted through parenteral, percutaneous, or mucosal exposure to infected bodily fluids.

topic: Infection Control - Hepatitis E Acute Case Duration
question: A mild case of Hepatitis E might last for which of the following numbers of days?
explanation: According to clinical epidemiological data and public health frameworks referenced in infection control standards, acute, uncomplicated cases of Hepatitis E (HEV) are typically self-limiting. A mild clinical presentation of the virus generally resolves spontaneously within a 7-14 day window as the host's immune system clears the viral load.

topic: Infection Control - Hepatitis B Post-Acute Fatigue and Depression Symptoms
question: Which of the following strains of Hepatitis may cause extreme fatigue and depression in the last stages of the disease?
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual (7th ed., p. 138), the acute phase of a Hepatitis B (HBV) infection—which features mild flu-like symptoms lasting two to six weeks—is frequently followed by a lingering period of extreme fatigue and depression that can persist for several months.

topic: Infection Control - Hepatitis C Incubation Period Standards
question: According to the CNT manual, which of the following incubation periods corresponds to Hepatitis C (HCV)?
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual, the established incubation period for the Hepatitis C virus (HCV) ranges from 14 to 180 days. This highly variable window reflects the slow, often asymptomatic prodromal profile of the pathogen before acute markers or chronic liver dysfunction manifest.

topic: Infection Control - Classification of Autogenous vs Cross Infections
question: Infections that are already in the body and have moved from one location to another have which of the following names?
explanation: According to epidemiology and the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual, an autogenous infection is defined as an infection caused by an infectious agent that the patient is already carrying, which is transferred from its normal, benign site to another part of the body where it can cause pathology. This is distinct from cross-infections, which originate from an external source or person.

topic: Infection Control - Hepatitis A Incubation Period Standards
question: According to the CNT manual, which of the following incubation periods corresponds to Hepatitis A (HAV)?
explanation: According to both the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual (7th ed.) and the CDC, the incubation period for the Hepatitis A virus (HAV) is 15-50 days, with a precise clinical average of 28 days. This enteric pathogen presents with a much shorter incubation window than chronic bloodborne pathogens.

topic: Infection Control - Clinical Symptomatology of Acute Hepatitis C
question: Which of the following symptoms do not correspond to acute Hepatitis C?
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual (7th ed., p. 139), individuals who manifest symptoms of acute Hepatitis C will experience joint aches, mild skin rash, loss of appetite, abdominal pain, darker urine, and light or grey-colored stools. Extreme fatigue is not explicitly listed among these acute phase manifestations, making it the non-corresponding option based on the text.

topic: Federal Regulations - OSHA Hepatitis B Vaccination Mandates
question: OSHA requires all employers to offer which of the following vaccinations to personnel performing invasive procedures or cleaning contaminated equipment?
explanation: According to the OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard (29 CFR 1910.1030), employers must make the Hepatitis B (HBV) vaccine series available at no cost to all employees who have occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials (OPIM). This mandate specifically covers personnel performing invasive procedures or processing contaminated clinical equipment due to the high environmental stability and transmission efficiency of HBV.

topic: Infection Control - Hepatitis B Environmental Stability and Surface Survival
question: For which of the following periods of time can HBV survive outside of the body?
explanation: According to the CDC and the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual, the Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is highly stable in the environment and can survive on inanimate objects and dry surfaces for at least 7 days while retaining its infectivity. This high level of resilience necessitates strict adherence to standard environmental disinfection protocols in clinical settings.

topic: Infection Control - Prevalence of Chronic Bloodborne Pathogens in the US
question: Which of the following chronic bloodborne viral infections is most common in the United States?
explanation: According to the CDC and public health data referenced in the CCAOM CNT Manual, Hepatitis C (HCV) is the most common chronic bloodborne viral infection in the United States. It affects millions of individuals nationwide, largely because its initial acute phase is frequently asymptomatic, allowing the virus to silently progress to a chronic carrier state before detection.

topic: Infection Control - Hepatitis E Incubation Period Guidelines
question: According to the CNT manual, which of the following incubation periods corresponds to Hepatitis E (HEV)?
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual, the incubation period for the Hepatitis E virus (HEV) ranges from 15 to 60 days, with an established clinical average of 40 days. Like HAV, this enteric virus features a much shorter and more acute incubation window than chronic bloodborne pathogens.

topic: Pathology - Chronic Hepatitis C Progression Statistics
question: Which of the following diseases is not considered an end-stage disease for people with chronic HCV?
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual (7th ed., p. 141), chronic Hepatitis C (HCV) infection commonly progresses to chronic hepatitis (chronic inflammation of the liver), with 5-20% of patients developing liver cirrhosis over 20 to 30 years and 1-5% developing hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer). Cholestasis is not listed among these tracked, characteristic stages or end-stage complications of the disease progression.

topic: Infection Control - Acute Hepatitis A Clinical Presentation
question: Which Hepatitis strain has abrupt onset symptoms of abdominal discomfort, loss of appetite, fatigue, nausea, dark urine, and jaundice?
explanation: According to the CCAOM Clean Needle Technique (CNT) Manual, Hepatitis A (HAV) is characterized by an acute, abrupt onset of symptoms following its incubation period. This clinical presentation classically includes sudden abdominal discomfort, anorexia (loss of appetite), fatigue, nausea, dark urine, and jaundice, differentiating its acute phase from the typically insidious or asymptomatic onset of bloodborne strains like HCV.

topic: Infection Control - Hepatitis B Post-Exposure Prophylaxis Standards
question: Which of the following treatments are used for HBV infection in the event of exposure?
options: HBV immune globulin and HBV vaccine
correct: HBV immune globulin and HBV vaccine
explanation: According to CDC guidelines and infection control protocols in the CCAOM CNT Manual, standard post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) for a suspected Hepatitis B (HBV) exposure involves a combined approach of passive and active immunization. Administering both Hepatitis B Immune Globulin (HBIG) for immediate antibody protection and initiating or completing the Hepatitis B vaccine series provides optimal protection against viral establishment. Direct-acting antivirals like Harvoni or Sovaldi are indicated solely for HCV.

topic: Immunology - Innate Physical and Chemical Barriers to Infection
question: Which of the following examples is not the body’s natural barrier to infection?
options: Intact skin and healthy respiratory mucosa
Stomach acid, tears, urine and vaginal secretions
Mucous membranes of the nose, throat, urethra, and rectum
Urine and vaginal secretions, broken skin in the mouth
correct: Urine and vaginal secretions, broken skin in the mouth
explanation: According to principles of immunology and clinical infection control, the body's natural defense barriers must be anatomically intact to prevent pathogen entry. Compromised epithelial tissue, such as broken skin or mucosal lesions in the oral cavity, serves as an active portal of entry for infectious agents rather than a defensive barrier. Normal secretions, intact dermis, and undamaged mucous membranes represent functional innate barriers.

topic: Infection Control - Mechanisms of Cross-Infection Transmission
question: Which of the following names is given to the type of infection that is transmitted from one person and passed on to another?
explanation: According to public health and infection control frameworks outlined in the CCAOM CNT Manual, a cross-infection occurs when an infectious pathogen is transmitted from one host or external vector to another individual.
