It is not classified as a criminal violation or federal statute breach by itself.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Neurological Assessment (Upper Extremity Reflexes)
question: A patient is examined and the brachioradialis deep tendon reflex is weak. Which cervical nerve root is most likely involved?
explanation: Deep tendon reflexes test specific spinal nerve roots. Tapping the brachioradialis tendon (on the forearm near the thumb side) tests the C6 nerve root. C5 and C6 handle the biceps reflex, C7 controls the triceps reflex, and C4/C8 do not have primary upper arm tendon reflexes.

topic: Clinical Assessment - Male Breast Mass & Hepatomegaly Diagnostics
question: Martin is a 64-year-old businessman who plays golf 2-3 times per week. After each game he has a couple of drinks with friends. He also drinks at home in the evening, 3-4 scotch and sodas every night and more on weekends. He complains that his breasts are enlarging. Examination reveals moderately prominent gynecomastia bilaterally. The left breast is larger than the right. Firmness can be felt in the left breast which is not present on the right. A cluster of 4-5 palpable nodes can be felt in the left axilla. No nodes can be felt on the right. His liver edge is 3 finger breadths below the right costal margin and moderately tender. The liver also percusses 4 finger breadths above the costal region. There is no sign of ascites nor jaundice. He reports that his urine is normal yellow color. What course of action should be taken?
options: Mammography, Liver Function tests, Full Chem Panel, Referral to surgeon
Secretin test, Liver Function tests, Full Chem Panel
Liver Function tests, Full Chem Panel
Liver Function tests, Full Chem Panel, Secretin test, Referral to surgeon
correct: Mammography, Liver Function tests, Full Chem Panel, Referral to surgeon
explanation: Although heavy alcohol use can cause enlarged breasts (gynecomastia) from liver trouble, a firm lump with swollen armpit lymph nodes on one side is a red flag for male breast cancer. Therefore, he needs a mammogram (breast X-ray) and a surgical referral to check the lump, as well as liver tests to check his liver function. A secretin test checks the pancreas and is not needed here.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Musculoskeletal & HEENT Assessment (TMJ Evaluation)
question: Upon inspection and palpation of the face, approximately one inch anterior to the external auditory meatus, you find swelling, tenderness and decreased range of jaw motion. This suggests
explanation: The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) connects your jawbone to your skull right in front of your ear canal (external auditory meatus). Inflammation in this joint causes swelling, tenderness just in front of the ear, and difficulty or pain when moving the jaw. Otitis media and otitis externa are ear infections inside or along the ear canal, while cellulitis is a spreading bacterial skin infection.

topic: Integration TCM + Biomed - Western Pharmacology & TCM Pattern Matching
question: A 22 year old female is prescribed Ortho Tri-Cyclen (estradiol/norgestimate). Which TCM disharmony would most likely apply?
options: painful menstruation due to stagnant Blood
skin itching due to hot blood
correct: painful menstruation due to stagnant Blood
explanation: Ortho Tri-Cyclen is a combination birth control pill commonly used to treat painful periods (dysmenorrhea) and irregular cycles. In Chinese Medicine, painful menstruation is caused by Blood Stasis (stagnant Blood) blocking the smooth flow of energy and blood in the uterus. The other options describe digestive weakness, bladder issues, or skin itching, which are not reasons to prescribe birth control pills.

topic: Infection Control - OSHA Regulations & Exposure Control Protocols
question: In a health care clinic, the Exposure Control Plan (ECP) should be reviewed
options: only when there are new health procedures
annually or when new procedures are added
correct: annually or when new procedures are added
explanation: OSHA safety standards require every healthcare clinic to review and update its Exposure Control Plan at least once every 12 months (annually), as well as whenever new procedures or positions are introduced that could change an employee's risk of exposure to bloodborne pathogens.

topic: Pharmacology - Gastrointestinal Therapeutics (Antidiarrheals)
question: Which of the following anti-diarrheal generic drugs are opioids?
explanation: Difenoxin, diphenoxylate, and loperamide are all opioid-class medications that slow down bowel motility by activating mu-opioid receptors in the gut wall. Attapulgite is not an opioid; it is an absorbent clay mineral that thickens stool by soaking up liquid.

topic: Decision-Making & Standard of Care - Malignancy Red Flags & Specialist Referral
question: Ray is a 46 year-old male who complains of a sore throat. For the past six weeks he says that he has had a cold. The history shows that he smokes 1.5 packs of cigarettes per day and drinks an average of four beers each night. Looking at the back of his throat shows some redness but no other abnormalities. He complains of difficulty swallowing and weight loss without being on a diet. When his neck is palpated several lymph nodes can be felt at the jugular lymph node chain. The lymph nodes are not tender. The rest of the physical exam is normal for his age. What is your course of action?
options: tell him that his cold will resolve itself
prescribe a series of acupuncture treatment
use an laryngoscope to look further into the throat
explanation: Heavy smoking and alcohol use combined with persistent dysphagia, unexplained weight loss, and non-tender swollen neck lymph nodes for 6 weeks are major red flags for throat or esophageal cancer. This patient needs an immediate, urgent referral to an oncologist or ENT specialist for evaluation. Performing laryngoscopy is outside an acupuncturist's scope, and treating with acupuncture or ignoring the symptoms delays life-saving care.

topic: Pharmacology - Psychotropic Medications (SSRIs)
question: A 45 year-old female is taking Zoloft (sertraline hydrochloride). What is the presenting problem?
explanation: Zoloft (sertraline) is a Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor (SSRI) used primarily for psychiatric conditions such as depression, anxiety, OCD, PTSD, and panic disorder. It has no indication for sleep apnea, viral infections, or cognitive disorders like dementia.

topic: Pharmacology - Rheumatology & Anti-Inflammatory Therapeutics
question: A 57 year-old male has Rheumatoid Arthritis. What categories of drugs can be prescribed?
explanation: Rheumatoid Arthritis is an autoimmune disorder managed with NSAIDs for immediate pain relief, DMARDs to slow down disease progression and joint damage, and Corticosteroids for quick control of acute flares. Antibiotics are for bacterial infections and do not treat autoimmune joint disease.

topic: Decision-Making & Standard of Care - Red Flag Triaging & Specialist Referral
question: A patient has weight loss, recurrent sweats, and fever. Which characteristics of the symptoms warrant a referral?
options: symptoms are unexplained and fluctuate over time
symptoms are unexplained and gradually worsen over time
symptoms are unexplained and stop and start over time
symptoms are unexplained and gradually worsen and then improve
correct: symptoms are unexplained and gradually worsen over time
explanation: Systemic symptoms such as unexplained weight loss, fever, and recurrent sweats are key red flags ('B-symptoms') for serious conditions like cancer or systemic infections. When these symptoms progressively worsen over time without a clear explanation, immediate medical evaluation and referral to a physician are required. Symptoms that improve or fluctuate are less suggestive of progressive underlying malignancy.

topic: Infection Control - Aftercare Hygiene & Antiseptic Care
question: A teenager has just pierced her earlobes. What can be done to prevent an infection?
options: wait a week before using earrings
regularly swab the earlobes with alcohol
correct: regularly swab the earlobes with alcohol
explanation: After getting earlobes pierced, proper skin hygiene is required to prevent bacterial infection. Cleaning the area regularly with an antiseptic solution like alcohol helps kill germs and keep the wound clean. Aspirin acts as a blood thinner and does not kill bacteria, delaying earrings allows the piercing hole to close, and massaging the area can introduce germs into the open skin wound.

topic: Clinical Assessment - Systemic Scleroderma Presentation
question: Systemic scleroderma is characterized by
options: thickening and hardening of the skin
correct: thickening and hardening of the skin
explanation: Scleroderma literally means 'hard skin.' It is an autoimmune disorder where excessive collagen builds up in the connective tissue, causing skin thickening, tightening, and hardening along with potential fibrosis of internal organs. It causes gut hypomotility (sluggish digestion) rather than hypermotility, and dermatomyositis is a separate muscle disease.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Neurological Assessment (Superficial Reflexes)
question: The upper abdominal reflex tests for
explanation: Superficial abdominal reflexes evaluate the integrity of the thoracic spinal cord. The upper abdominal reflex (stroking the skin above the umbilicus toward the center) evaluates upper thoracic roots T8–T10 (or T9–T11), while the lower abdominal reflex tests lower thoracic roots T10–T12.

topic: Decision-Making & Standard of Care - Asthma Exacerbation & Referral Triage
question: A 38 year-old male presented with mild and occasional SOB for the past several weeks. Recently, he has had a cough with severe SOB. Upon asking, he reported no chest pain, fever, or bloody sputum. History included asthma which required emergency treatment on several occasions. He has stopped using his inhalers as he was feeling much better. Blood pressure was 120/78 and heart sounds were normal. Lung sounds were normal at rest respiration but positive for wheezing on a forced exhale. Which action would you take?
options: advise patient to avoid allergens, refer to a nutritionist
have family member transport patient to emergency department (ED)
urgent (same day) referral to their primary care physician
correct: urgent (same day) referral to their primary care physician
explanation: A patient with an asthma history who stopped taking his inhalers and presents with wheezing and worsening shortness of breath needs same-day medical attention to restart medication. Since his resting respiration and blood pressure are stable without signs of emergency failure, an urgent (same-day) PCP referral is appropriate rather than calling 911.

topic: Clinical Assessment - Obstetrics & Gynecological Pathology (Ectopic Pregnancy)
question: A pelvic ultrasonography can be used to detect extrauterine pregnancies. What is accurate about extrauterine pregnancies?
options: Bleeding is a major concern, 80 percent occur on the ovary
70 percent occur in the cervix, Mostly occur in women 20-30 years old, Bleeding is a major concern
90 percent occur in the fallopian tubes, Mostly occur in women 35-44 years old, Bleeding is a major concern
Emergency situation when associated with abdominal pain with vaginal light bleeding, 60 percent occur in the abdominal cavity
correct: 90 percent occur in the fallopian tubes, Mostly occur in women 35-44 years old, Bleeding is a major concern
explanation: Extrauterine (ectopic) pregnancies occur when an egg implants outside the uterus. Over 90% of ectopic pregnancies take place in the fallopian tubes. They occur most commonly in women aged 35–44, and internal bleeding/hemorrhage from a ruptured tube is a major life-threatening complication. Cervical, ovarian, and abdominal sites make up only a tiny percentage of cases.

topic: Anatomy & Physiology - Endocrine System (Thyroid Axis & TSH Function)
question: Thyrotropin (or TSH) stimulates the thyroid gland to release
explanation: Thyrotropin, also known as Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone (TSH), is released by the anterior pituitary gland to signal the thyroid gland to produce thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3). Parathormone comes from the parathyroid glands, thymosin comes from the thymus, and calcitonin is released by thyroid C-cells in response to serum calcium levels, not TSH.

topic: Anatomy & Physiology - Endocrine System (Adrenal Cortex Pathology)
question: A 43 year-old female has Addison's Disease. What are her symptoms?
options: fatigue, loss of memory, poor concentration, enlarged lymph nodes, unrefreshing sleep, unexplained muscle pain
weakness, hypotension, hyperpigmentation, craving salt, vitiligo, cold intolerance, anorexia
milky white patches on the skin, premature graying of hair, loss of color in mucous membranes
dizziness, blurred vision, cold and clammy skin, rapid and shallow breathing, fatigue
correct: weakness, hypotension, hyperpigmentation, craving salt, vitiligo, cold intolerance, anorexia
explanation: Addison's disease is primary adrenal insufficiency (lack of cortisol and aldosterone). Low cortisol causes weakness, anorexia, and cold intolerance, while high ACTH causes hyperpigmentation. Low aldosterone causes sodium loss, leading to hypotension and salt cravings. Vitiligo often co-occurs as an autoimmune finding. CFS presents with unrefreshing sleep and enlarged nodes, while vitiligo alone is limited to skin depigmentation.

topic: Clinical Assessment - Gastroenterology & Red Flag Pathology (Colorectal Malignancy)
question: Jennifer is a 52 year-old factory worker... What is your presumptive diagnosis?
explanation: Unintentional weight loss, unexplained fatigue, high red meat diet, and hematochezia (rectal bleeding) combined with deep pelvic/back pain and normal spinal exam findings are primary red flags for colorectal cancer. Hemorrhoids cause bleeding but not systemic weight loss, and structural back conditions do not cause GI bleeding.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Cardiovascular Assessment (Blood Pressure Classification)
question: Blood pressure 140-159/90-99 is considered
explanation: In hypertension stage 2 the systolic blood pressure is between 140 and 159 or the diastolic pressure is between 90 and 99. In stage 1 hypertension lifestyle changes are recommended plus the need to take medication, usually a thiazide-type diuretic. Normal BP: Less than 120/80 mm Hg. Elevated: Systolic between 120-129 and diastolic less than 80. Stage 1: Systolic between 130-139 or diastolic between 80-89. Stage 2: Systolic at least 140 or diastolic at least 90 mm Hg. Hypertensive crisis: Systolic over 180 and/or diastolic over 120, with patients needing prompt changes in medication if there are no other indications of problems, or immediate hospitalization if there are signs of organ damage. The guidelines eliminate the category of prehypertension, categorizing patients as having either Elevated (120-129 and less than 80) or Stage I hypertension (130-139 or 80-89). Previous guidelines classified 140/90 mm Hg as Stage 1 hypertension.

topic: Anatomy & Physiology - Endocrine System (Adrenal Function & Cortisol)
question: Decreased levels of cortisol are found in
explanation: Addison's disease is primary adrenal insufficiency, where the adrenal glands produce insufficient amounts of steroid hormones, leading to abnormally low cortisol levels. Cushing's disease is characterized by hypercortisolism (excessive cortisol). Hyperthyroidism affects thyroid hormone levels, and obesity does not cause adrenal insufficiency.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Diagnostic Imaging & Laboratory Workup
question: Pulmonary Angiography is indicated most commonly in patients with suspected
explanation: Pulmonary angiography is a specialized fluoroscopic imaging procedure that visualizes blood flow through the pulmonary arteries. Its primary medical indication is to detect filling defects or blockages caused by a pulmonary embolism (PE). Emphysema, pneumonia, and tuberculosis are diagnosed using chest X-rays, CT scans, sputum cultures, or pulmonary function tests.

topic: Decision-Making & Standard of Care - Abdominal Pain Triage & Immediate Care Indications
question: A 33 year-old female patient has constant abdominal pain. Which symptoms associated with the abdominal pain would allow you to conclude that she can be treated now?
options: Unremitting sharp pain starts in back near the ribs and moves down toward the groin, fever
Fever, right lower abdomen pain with superficial and deep tenderness
Pain starts in right abdomen, shift to back, and worsens with fatty meals
correct: Pain starts in right abdomen, shift to back, and worsens with fatty meals
explanation: Uncomplicated biliary pain (right-upper quadrant pain radiating to the back worsened by fatty foods) is non-emergent and can be treated in an outpatient acupuncture setting. Fever with kidney pain/flank pain, acute appendicitis (RLQ pain/fever), and vaginal bleeding in pregnancy are medical emergencies requiring immediate emergency referral.

topic: Office Management & Legal Requirements - Confidentiality & Release of PHI
question: What is the procedure of releasing confidential information?
options: Identify who is to receive information, Have patient sign and date release, Send the original records
Define what information is to be released, Have patient sign and date release
Define what information is to be released, Identify who is to receive information, Have patient sign and date release, Send the original records
Define what information is to be released, Identify who is to receive information, Have patient sign and date release
correct: Define what information is to be released, Identify who is to receive information, Have patient sign and date release
explanation: Releasing confidential medical information requires a signed and dated release form specifying both the exact information being disclosed and the designated recipient. Original medical records are always retained by the practice; only copies are provided.

topic: Anatomy & Physiology - Endocrine & Renal Systems (RAAS Pathway)
question: Angiotensin II stimulates the secretion of the hormone
explanation: Angiotensin II is a key peptide hormone in the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS). It acts directly on the adrenal cortex to trigger the secretion of aldosterone, which regulates blood pressure and fluid balance by causing the kidneys to retain sodium and water.

topic: Obstetric & Gynecologic Pathologies - Maternal Smoking Risks
question: Women who smoke during pregnancy have a greater risk of
explanation: Smoking during pregnancy reduces oxygen and blood flow to the baby. This often leads to delivering the baby too early (prematurely) and the baby being born under weight. Smoking makes babies smaller, not heavier, and while smoke exposure later can harm lungs, early birth is the primary birth risk.

topic: Federal Regulations - HIPAA Privacy & Emancipated Minors
question: You are treating a 16 year-old emancipated minor with acupuncture. His father contacts you and wants to have access to the medical records because of insurance. What do you do?
options: He is the father and can legally get the release
The father needs the son to authorize the release
The answer varies from state to state
Call the insurance company for advice
correct: The father needs the son to authorize the release
explanation: An emancipated minor has the legal rights of an adult when it comes to medical privacy. Even though he is under 18, his parents no longer have an automatic right to see his medical records. The provider needs written permission from the son himself before sharing any information with the father.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Lower Extremity Musculoskeletal Anatomy
question: The gastrocnemius muscle and soleus unit along with the posterior tibialis and toe flexors hallucis longus and digitorum longus are involved with which motion of the foot and ankle?
explanation: Plantar flexion means pointing your foot downward, like standing on your tiptoes. All the muscles listed run down the back of the lower leg and ankle, pulling the heel up or the toes down. Dorsiflexion is lifting the foot up, inversion turns the foot in, and eversion turns the foot out.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Diagnostic Laboratory Tests (Pregnanediol)
question: Urinary pregnanediol is measured to evaluate
explanation: Pregnanediol is the waste product created when the body breaks down progesterone. Because it comes out in the urine, doctors can measure urinary pregnanediol to check if a person is making enough progesterone, which helps confirm if ovulation has occurred. The other options are different hormones with entirely different waste products.

topic: Clinical Assessment - Fever of Unknown Origin & Red Flags
question: Fever of 101.5 degrees F of unknown origin is a red flag for
explanation: A high fever without a clear cause is a red flag that points to something serious hidden in the body. The most common underlying causes are hidden (occult) infections or autoimmune diseases where the immune system attacks its own tissue. Conditions like fibromyalgia or chronic fatigue do not cause high fevers.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Diagnostic Exams & Pulmonary Function Tests
question: A spirometer is a machine that can measure
explanation: A spirometer is a medical device that measures how much air you can breathe into your lungs and how quickly you can blow it out. It tests lung function and capacity. Joint movement is measured with a goniometer, esophageal issues with manometry, and bladder capacity with ultrasound or cystometry.

topic: Decision-Making & Standard of Care - Red Flag Referrals & Emergencies
question: Glen is 17 years old with type 1 diabetes. He is on variable amounts of insulin per day. One hot day in July, Glen goes swimming at a hot springs. The next day he develops fever, dizziness, right ear pain, and tinnitus. The doctor gives him amoxicillin for a middle ear infection. The next day he is worse with purulent drainage from his right ear, worsening dizziness, severe headache, and a temperature of 103 degrees F. He is disoriented and somnolent. What is the next course of action?
options: New drug prescription, bed rest with plenty of fluids
explanation: This patient has Type 1 diabetes and developed a severe ear infection that spread, causing high fever, intense headache, confusion, and extreme sleepiness (somnolence). These severe symptoms mean the infection may have reached his brain or skull bone, which is a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate hospital admission for IV drugs and emergency tests.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Diagnostic Exams & Procedures
question: Which test is used to evaluate patients with seizures or brain tumors?
explanation: An EEG (electroencephalogram) records brain waves by placing small sensors on the scalp. It is used to check brain electrical activity to diagnose seizures and brain tumors. An ECG checks the heart, an ENG checks balance and eye movements, and an EMG tests muscles and peripheral nerves.

topic: Breast cancer
question: A mammography report of Class V is
options: Suspicious for cancer; further evaluation suggested
explanation: The American College of Radiology (ACR) has standardized the results for mammograms. Class I is negative, class II is benign, class III is benign but short-term follow-up is suggested, Class IV is suspicious for cancer with further evaluation suggested, Class V indicates that cancer is highly suspected, Class VI indicates that it is a known biopsy-proven malignancy. Because of false-positives, mammograms do not confirm the presence of breast cancer. Abnormal mammograms are followed up with additional testing (diagnostic mammograms, ultrasound, biopsy) to detect the cancer. Diagnostic mammography takes longer to do than screening mammography because more x-ray images are taken.

topic: Infection Control - Biohazardous Regulated Waste Handling
question: Regulated waste as a category of biohazardous medical waste requires special
options: storage, blue color labeling, and disposal
explanation: Regulated medical waste (like blood-soaked items or used needles) must be safely handled from start to finish. This means keeping it in safe storage containers, putting biohazard labels on it so everyone knows it is dangerous, and disposing of it through licensed services. Blue is not the color used for biohazards (red or orange is).

topic: Ethics & Professionalism - Informed Consent Requirements
question: What is included in an informed consent?
options: Explain the medical procedures, Provide practitioner names for therapeutic alternatives
Describe the potential risks from the procedure
Explain the medical procedures, Describe the potential risks from the procedure
Explain the medical procedures, Describe the potential risks from the procedure, Present therapeutic alternatives
correct: Explain the medical procedures, Describe the potential risks from the procedure, Present therapeutic alternatives
explanation: Informed consent means a patient fully understands what will happen before agreeing to treatment. To be valid, the practitioner must explain the procedure, describe the potential risks, and discuss other available treatment options (therapeutic alternatives). Leaving out alternatives or risks makes the consent incomplete.

topic: Pharmacology - Central Nervous System Drugs (Alzheimer Disease)
question: An 82-year old male has Alzheimer Disease. What is the treatment?
explanation: Alzheimer's disease reduces acetylcholine, a chemical messenger in the brain needed for memory. Cholinesterase inhibitors like Aricept block the enzyme that breaks down acetylcholine, helping brain cells communicate better. The other options are incorrect drug classes or mislabeled medications that do not treat core Alzheimer's disease.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Diagnostic Studies & Cardiac Evaluation
question: Dennis is a 74-year-old retired physician. He has a diagnosis of entrapment of the ulnar nerve on his right arm. He has no positive cardiac history and is not taking any medications. He does not smoke and drinks 1-2 glasses of wine in the evening. While fishing, he was stung in the neck by a hornet. He fell into the pond with all his clothes on, into the icy water. Swimming to shore, he experienced a pounding in his chest which continued after he arrived onshore. There was no pain. He felt his pulse and it felt thready and could not count his heartbeats as they are very fast. Dressing in warm clothes, he later arrives to your office and says that he is having a heart attack. What further diagnostic studies should be done first?
explanation: When a patient experiences a sudden abnormally fast heartbeat (tachycardia) or chest pounding, the very first test needed is an ECG (electrocardiogram). An ECG records the heart's electrical activity in real time to show what kind of irregular rhythm is happening. Blood tests and chest X-rays can follow later, but evaluating heart rhythm comes first.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Musculoskeletal & Neuromuscular Pathologies
question: Parker is 13 years old. His father says that Parker is getting weaker rather than stronger. Parker is tall for his age. He is about six feet and powerfully built. His weight is about 200 pounds. Parker loves gymnastics and works out in the gym every afternoon to build his pecs, shoulders, and quads. He takes protein supplements. He says that he was once able to press 150 pounds and now can only press 100 pounds. He says that his muscles are still big but they are getting weaker. He says that he sleeps in an upper bunk but now has trouble climbing to reach it. Parker says that he does not want to become like his uncle who had to get married in a wheelchair and died when he was 45. Based on history alone, what is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Muscular dystrophy is a genetic disease that causes muscles to slowly get weaker over time, even if they still look big (pseudohypertrophy). The family story about his uncle dying young in a wheelchair points to an inherited muscle-wasting disease. Crohn's is an bowel disease, Charcot-Marie-Tooth affects nerve ends in hands/feet, and Thalassemia is a blood disorder.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Cranial Nerves Anatomy & Physiology
question: Which cranial nerve controls the eyelid and eyeball movement ?
explanation: Cranial Nerve III (Oculomotor nerve) acts like the steering wheel and power switch for your eye. It lifts your upper eyelid and moves your eyeball up, down, and inward. Cranial Nerve II handles vision/seeing, Cranial Nerve X controls internal organs, and Cranial Nerve XI moves neck and shoulder muscles.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Diagnostic Laboratory Tests (Thyroid Panel)
question: High TSH levels mean
explanation: TSH (Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone) is the brain's message telling the thyroid gland to work harder. If the thyroid gland is slow and underactive (hypothyroidism), the brain pumps out high levels of TSH to try to kickstart it. Amyloidosis is protein buildup, Cushing's involves high cortisol, and Addison's involves low adrenal hormones.

topic: Integration TCM + Biomed - Cross-Referencing Biomedical Drugs & TCM Pattern
question: A 27-year old male is prescribed Valtrex (valacyclovir). Which TCM disharmony would most likely apply?
options: insomnia due to liver and gall bladder fire
explanation: Valtrex is an antiviral drug used to treat herpes infections, such as genital herpes. In Chinese medicine, painful, red, fluid-filled blisters in the lower body are classified as Damp-Heat. Bi syndrome affects joints, insomnia affects sleep, and sinusitis affects nasal passages.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Musculoskeletal Physical Exam (Hip & Pelvis)
question: While examining a patient for placement of the needle at GB-30, you happen to flex the hip and internally rotate, palpating the tissue, you find swelling, tenderness, and pain. This suggests.
explanation: GB-30 is located right over the greater trochanter of the thigh bone. The trochanteric bursa is a fluid-filled sac sitting right over this bone. When it gets inflamed (trochanteric bursitis), pressing on the area or moving the hip (flexion and internal rotation) compresses the bursa, causing localized swelling, tenderness, and pain.

topic: Psychiatric & Substance Use Pathologies - Cannabis/Marijuana Abuse
question: A 19 year-old female talks loudly and laughs inappropriately during the interview. She reports of often feeling confused and feeling unmotivated to complete college. She reports that she gained weight. Her eyes appear glassy and bright. You suspect drug abuse of
explanation: Marijuana use often causes inappropriate laughter, loud speech, glassy eyes, increased appetite (leading to weight gain), and a loss of drive or motivation (amotivational syndrome). Heroin causes pinpoint pupils and drowsiness, inhalants leave chemical smells/sores, and depressants slow everything down without causing weight gain and inappropriate laughter.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Complete Blood Count (WBC Count)
question: A high WBC count indicates
explanation: White blood cells (WBCs) are the body's immune defense soldiers. When you get an infection, your body makes many extra white blood cells to fight off the germs, leading to a high WBC count. Leukopenia means a low WBC count, anemia means low red blood cells, and heart failure is measured with different heart tests.

topic: Infectious Pathologies - Viral Exanthems & Nomenclature
question: Varicella is another term for
explanation: Varicella is the formal medical term for chicken pox, a common viral illness that causes an itchy blister-like rash. Mumps causes swollen salivary glands, tonsillitis is inflamed tonsils, and measles is known as rubeola.

topic: Pharmacology - Antibiotic Administration & Interactions (Tetracyclines)
question: For optimal effect, tetracycline should be given
options: Only in the morning before breakfast
explanation: Tetracycline needs an empty stomach to absorb properly into your blood. Food and dairy products (like milk) contain calcium and other minerals that bind to tetracycline, blocking it from working. Taking it one hour before meals with plain water ensures the body absorbs the full dose.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Lower Extremity Musculoskeletal Anatomy
question: The following muscles of the leg and foot: anterior tibialis, toe extensors, hallucis longus and digitorum longus, are involved in which motion of the ankle?
explanation: Dorsiflexion means lifting your foot and toes upward toward your shin. All the muscles listed run down the front (anterior) part of your leg and pull the top of the foot up. Plantar flexion points the foot down, inversion turns it inward, and eversion turns it outward.

topic: Cardiovascular Pathologies - Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm (AAA)
question: For the past two weeks a 70 year-old male patient has been feeling a "pounding" in his abdomen. He says that it feels like his heart is in his stomach. After retirement five years ago he says that he has gained over 50 pounds, mostly around his abdomen. He reports no other current symptoms but says that he has had three skin cancer lesions removed in the past five years. Deep palpation of the abdomen reveals a prominent lateral aortic pulsation in the back of the abdomen. The femoral, popliteal, and pedal pulses are normal. There are no ischemic signs of his feet. He denies smoking and drinking. Urination, appetite, and bowel movements are normal. What is the presumptive diagnosis?
explanation: An abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is an enlargement or bulging of the main artery passing through the stomach area. Patients often feel a pounding heartbeat in their stomach. On physical exam, doctors can feel a distinct lateral pulsing (heartbeat movement spreading sideways) deep in the abdomen. Ascites is fluid buildup, aortic valve disorder involves heart valves, and interstitial cystitis is a bladder condition.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Diagnostic Exams & Spinal Tap Procedure
question: A lumbar or spinal puncture analyzes
explanation: A lumbar puncture (spinal tap) places a needle into the lower back to draw out cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), the protective liquid surrounding the brain and spinal cord. Gastric fluid comes from the stomach, synovial fluid comes from joints (arthrocentesis), and peritoneal fluid comes from the belly (paracentesis).

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Complete Blood Count (RBC Indices)
question: The Red Blood Cell Indices (RBC Indices) test is useful in classifying
explanation: RBC indices measure the size, volume, and hemoglobin concentration of individual red blood cells (like MCV and MCH). Doctors use these measurements specifically to classify different types of anemia (such as microcytic or macrocytic anemia). Heart disease, leukemias, and bone marrow failure are evaluated with entirely different cardiac or bone marrow tests.

topic: Pharmacology - Central Nervous System & Antipsychotic Drugs
question: Which of the following is a first-generation antipsychotic drug?
explanation: First-generation (typical) antipsychotics like Haloperidol (Haldol) work mainly by blocking dopamine D2 receptors and are older medications with a higher risk of movement side effects (extrapyramidal symptoms). Zyprexa, Risperdal, and Abilify are all second-generation (atypical) antipsychotics that affect both serotonin and dopamine with lower risks of movement disorders.

topic: Pharmacology - Prescription Abbreviations & Terminology
question: In a drug prescription the abbreviation "TID" means
explanation: Medical prescription abbreviations come from Latin. TID stands for "ter in die," which means three times a day. BID means twice a day, and QOD means every other day (every second day).

topic: Neuromuscular & Musculoskeletal Pathologies - Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
question: A 55 year-old female is seen complaining of bilateral parasthesia and pain in the wrist that radiates from the forearm to the wrist. Her symptoms are worse on her right hand. She is right hand dominant. Symptoms are exacerbated when she is driving and keyboarding. This has been going on for 3 months. During that time she has found a method of shaking or wringing her hand to alleviate her symptoms. What is her diagnosis based on this history?
explanation: Carpal tunnel syndrome happens when the median nerve gets squeezed at the wrist. It causes numbness, tingling, and pain that gets worse with repetitive tasks like driving or typing. Patients classicly get relief by shaking out or wringing their hands (known as the "flick sign"). Cervical radiculopathy starts in the neck, tenosynovitis is tendon inflammation without paresthesia patterns, and brachial plexopathy affects the entire arm/shoulder plexus.

topic: Reproductive & Urological Pathologies - Prostate Cancer Metastasis
question: A 59 year-old patient, a taxi driver, states that during the last few weeks of prolonged sitting he has been experiencing stiffness and dull-deep pain in the lower back and pelvis. Rest provides some relief. The back and hip area are tender to the touch. He reports some weight loss, without being on a diet, fatigue, and nausea. He reports frequent difficult urination at night and painful ejaculation. The patient denied having local bruising or any radiation into the lower extremities. Coughing and sneezing did not trigger the pain. The pain is most likely due to
explanation: Prostate issues cause urinary problems like waking up at night to pee and painful ejaculation. When prostate cancer spreads (metastasizes), it usually spreads to the lower back and pelvic bones, causing deep bone pain, tenderness, and weight loss. BPH does not cause bone pain or weight loss, pyelonephritis causes high fever and flank pain, and spinal stenosis affects leg walking tolerance.

topic: Cardiovascular Pathologies - Buerger's Disease (Thromboangiitis Obliterans)
question: Palpating the pulses of the lower extremities on a patient with Buerger's disease would show that the pulses are
explanation: Buerger's disease causes inflammation and blood clots that block small blood vessels in the hands and feet (usually in smokers). Because the blood vessels are blocked, blood cannot flow down to the ankles and feet easily, making lower leg pulses very weak or impossible to feel.

topic: Cardiovascular Pathologies - Clinical Presentation of Acute Myocardial Infarction
question: The classic symptoms and signs of a heart attack include chest pain and radiating pain to shoulder, neck or arm. The secondary symptoms and signs of a heart attack include dizziness, nausea, sweating, and shortness of breath. What is the general difference of men having a heart attack versus women having a heart attack?
options: men have stronger classic than secondary symptoms and women have milder classic and more secondary
both men and women have stronger classic symptoms and signs than the secondary symptoms and signs
both men and women have stronger secondary symptoms and signs than the classic symptoms and signs
men and women have equally strong classic and equally strong secondary symptoms and signs
correct: men have stronger classic than secondary symptoms and women have milder classic and more secondary
explanation: Men typically display classic heart attack symptoms like severe chest pain and arm radiation. Women are statistically more likely to present with atypical or secondary symptoms such as nausea, shortness of breath, back pain, and fatigue, often with milder chest pain.

topic: Reproductive & Gynecological Pathologies - Vaginitis & Vaginal Infections
question: A 23 year-old woman has frothy yellow vaginal discharge with a foul odor. The wet mount test is positive for the flagellated protozoan parasite. NAAT (nucleic acid amplification test) is also positive. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Trichomonas vaginitis is a sexually transmitted infection caused by a single-celled, flagellated protozoan parasite. It classicly causes a frothy yellow-green, foul-smelling vaginal discharge. Bacterial vaginosis features clue cells, candidal vaginitis shows yeast/pseudohyphae with cottage-cheese discharge, and atrophic vaginitis is due to low estrogen.

topic: Patient Care & Safety - CPR & Emergency Procedures
question: For a one person rescue, what is the breaths-to-compressions ratio for either an adult, child, or infant?
explanation: For a single (one-person) rescuer, CPR guidelines mandate a standard ratio of 30 chest compressions to 2 rescue breaths (30:2) across all patients (adults, children, and infants). A 15:2 ratio is only used when two rescuers are performing CPR on an infant or child.

topic: Pharmacology - Respiratory & Allergy Medications (Nasal Corticosteroids)
question: A 22 year-old male is taking Nasonex (mometasone). What is the chief complaint?
explanation: Nasonex (mometasone furoate) is a corticosteroid nasal spray used to prevent and treat allergic rhinitis (allergies). Epistaxis (nosebleeds) is a potential side effect of nasal sprays, glossitis affects the tongue, and cystitis is a bladder condition.

topic: Patient Care & Safety - Safety, Infection Control & Clean Needle Technique
question: What is the most important procedure for preventing an infection in a health care setting?
options: Sterilization of all equipment that pierces the skin
explanation: According to the CDC, WHO, and Clean Needle Technique (CNT) manuals, hand washing is universally recognized as the single most effective and important procedure for preventing healthcare-associated infections and cross-contamination. While disposable needles and a clean field are critical for CNT, hand hygiene is the primary line of defense.

topic: Neuromuscular & Musculoskeletal Pathologies - Classification of Headaches
question: Sinus headaches are considered
explanation: Headaches are divided into primary and secondary. Primary headaches (like migraines or tension headaches) have no underlying disease cause. Secondary headaches are caused by an underlying condition—in this case, sinus inflammation/infection (rhinosinusitis). Tertiary is not a recognized classification, and rebound headaches are caused by medication overuse.

topic: Pharmacology - Respiratory Medications (Asthma Therapies)
question: Which of the following asthma drugs is an example of a short-acting beta-agonist drug?
explanation: Ventolin (albuterol) is a short-acting beta-agonist (SABA) used as a fast-acting rescue inhaler for acute asthma attacks. Accolate and Singulair are leukotriene receptor antagonists, and Zyflo is a 5-lipoxygenase inhibitor, all of which are daily controller medications rather than fast-acting bronchodilators.

topic: Patient Care & Safety - Medical Ethics, HIPAA & Patient Records Access
question: When a patient requests access to their medical records which of the following is accurate?
options: The original medical record must always be provided
A copy of the record can be provided, A fee must be agreed to in advance
The original medical record must always be provided, A fee must be agreed to in advance
A fee must be agreed to in advance
correct: A copy of the record can be provided, A fee must be agreed to in advance
explanation: Patients have a right to access their medical information, but clinics retain original paper/electronic files for legal compliance. Therefore, clinics provide copies (or summaries) of records, and any standard administrative or copying fees must be disclosed and agreed upon in advance.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Diagnostic Exams & Urinalysis
question: One of the purposes of the urine test is to assess the functioning of the adrenals by testing for
explanation: Cortisol is a key glucocorticoid hormone produced by the adrenal glands. A 24-hour free cortisol urine test measures urine cortisol to assess adrenal gland performance (such as detecting Cushing's syndrome). Sodium and chloride evaluate kidney fluid balance, while glucose evaluates diabetes/blood sugar regulation.

topic: Endocrine & Metabolic Pathologies - Diabetes Mellitus & Secondary Incontinence
question: An 11 year-old female was brought to the clinic by her mother. The child has been having what she calls "accidents" where she loses control of her bladder during the day and also at night. She is embarrassed in explaining her problem. She says that she has frequent and urgent urges to urinate and denies dysuria or hematuria. The mother says that she has had a weak bladder for the past two weeks. She also says that she has stomach aches but denies vomiting/diarrhea, flank pain, rashes, or breathing problems. She has normal bowel movements and sleep. She is not on any medication. She is 60 inches tall and weighs 160 pounds. BP is 104/60; HR is 80 bpm; RR is 16 rpm; temperature is 98.6 F. HEENT is normal. Lab tests were done with the following results: HbA1c: 8.4; Urine culture neg; after 48 hours; Urine dipstick (clean catch): pH = 6, Specific gravity = 1.015; Protein: negative; Glucose: positive. Ketones: neg; Nitrites: neg; Bilirubin: neg; Blood: neg. TSH = 2.6 uIU/ml; Two hour plasma glucose: 243. What is the most likely diagnosis for her incontinence?
explanation: This patient has clear laboratory markers for diabetes mellitus, including an HbA1c of 8.4% (normal < 5.7%) and a 2-hour plasma glucose of 243 mg/dL (normal < 140 mg/dL). High blood sugar causes glucose to spill into the urine (glucosuria), which acts as an osmotic diuretic leading to frequent urination and incontinence accidents. Normal TSH rules out thyroid disease, and negative urine culture rules out UTI.

topic: Endocrine & Metabolic Pathologies - Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Risk Factors
question: Risk factors for developing type 2 diabetes include obesity, hypertension, family history, and
explanation: Major metabolic risk factors for type 2 diabetes include obesity, physical inactivity, high blood pressure, family history, and dyslipidemia (specifically high triglycerides and low HDL cholesterol). Low BMI, high HDL, and low RBCs do not increase diabetes risk.

topic: Pharmacology - Gastrointestinal Medications (Antacids vs H2 Blockers)
question: OTC antacids that act by neutralizing stomach acid may contain which of the following ingredients in combination?
options: Calcium carbonate, Cimetidine, Magnesium hydroxide, Aluminum hydroxide
Calcium carbonate, Magnesium hydroxide, Aluminum hydroxide
correct: Calcium carbonate, Magnesium hydroxide, Aluminum hydroxide
explanation: Chemical antacids work directly by neutralizing gastric hydrochloric acid. Common antacid active bases include calcium carbonate, magnesium hydroxide, and aluminum hydroxide. Cimetidine (Tagamet) is an H2-receptor antagonist that decreases acid production rather than neutralizing acid directly.

topic: Pharmacology - Drug Naming Conventions & Suffixes
question: The generic name for beta-blocker drugs all end with
explanation: Generic drug stems (suffixes) indicate their pharmacological class. Beta-blockers end in "-olol" (e.g., metoprolol, atenolol). Drug names ending in "-terol" are beta-agonist bronchodilators, "-trel" are progestins, and "-triptan" are antimigraine serotonin agonists.

topic: Neuromuscular & Musculoskeletal Pathologies - Cranial Nerves (CN VIII)
question: Which of the following correctly describes the function of Cranial Nerve VIII (Vestibulocochlear nerve)?
options: Motor: facial expression / Sensation: taste (anterior 2/3 of tongue)
Motor: shoulder elevation / Sensation: skin over angle of jaw
Sensory: hearing and balance / Motor: none
correct: Sensory: hearing and balance / Motor: none
explanation: Cranial Nerve VIII (Vestibulocochlear nerve) is purely sensory. Its cochlear component mediates hearing and its vestibular component mediates balance and equilibrium. CN III, IV, and VI control eye movements; CN VII controls facial expressions and anterior tongue taste; CN XI controls shoulder elevation (trapezius).

topic: Pharmacology - OTC Analgesics & Caffeine Adjuvants
question: Which of the following brand names contain caffeine?
options: Excedrin Extra Strength, Midol Menstrual Formula, Advil
Excedrin Extra Strength, Midol Menstrual Formula, Anacin
correct: Excedrin Extra Strength, Midol Menstrual Formula, Anacin
explanation: Excedrin Extra Strength (acetaminophen + aspirin + caffeine), Midol Menstrual Formula (acetaminophen + pyrilamine + caffeine), and Anacin (aspirin + caffeine) all contain caffeine as an active ingredient. Standard Advil contains only ibuprofen and has no caffeine.

topic: Patient Care & Safety - Safety, Infection Control & Clean Needle Technique
question: In an acupuncture practice, when is it recommended that gloves be worn?
options: when bleeding is likely to occur, when needling near the genitals, when acupuncturist's hand has a cut
when acupuncturist 's hand has a cut, when bleeding is likely to occur
when inserting intradermal needles, when bleeding is likely to occur
when needling near the genitals, when inserting intradermal needles, when bleeding is likely to occur
correct: when bleeding is likely to occur, when needling near the genitals, when acupuncturist's hand has a cut
explanation: This is the most complete answer. Gloves need to be worn only under specific conditions where there can be exposure to blood and other potentially infected body fluids. It is also recommended to wear gloves when needling in the mouth, when palpating the patient's skin when there are cuts or lesions, when cleaning blood or other potentially infected fluids from a surface in the office. It is not necessary to wear gloves when inserting an intradermal needle when the skin barrier is intact.

topic: Gastrointestinal & Hepatic Pathologies - Hepatitis B Clinical Presentation
question: Hepatitis B symptoms include
options: diarrhea and abdominal pain, bloody stools
nausea and malaise, diarrhea and abdominal pain, bloody stools
chills and fever,  diarrhea and abdominal pain
chills and fever, nausea and malaise, diarrhea and abdominal pain
correct: chills and fever, nausea and malaise, diarrhea and abdominal pain
explanation: Acute Hepatitis B causes systemic flu-like and GI symptoms, including chills, fever, malaise, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. Bloody stools are not a symptom of viral hepatitis and indicate lower GI bleeding.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Cranial Nerves (CN IX & CN X)
question: The glossopharyngeal nerve is a ____________ nerve and the vagus nerve is a ____________nerve.
options: sensory and motor / sensory and motor
correct: sensory and motor / sensory and motor
explanation: Both the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX) and the vagus nerve (CN X) are mixed nerves, meaning they carry both sensory (feeling) signals back to the brain and motor (movement/action) signals to muscles and glands. CN IX helps you taste and swallow, while CN X helps control internal organs like your heart and stomach in addition to muscles in your throat. Because both nerves handle both jobs, the correct combination is sensory and motor for both.

topic: Urologic Pathologies - Prostate Cancer Presentation
question: A 57 year-old male has the diagnosis of Prostate Cancer. What are his symptoms?
options: urine reflux, perineal pain, prostate spasm
explanation: Prostate cancer causes symptoms by blocking urine flow or spreading to nearby bones. Growth in the prostate causes dysuria (painful urination) and hematuria (blood in the urine). When prostate cancer spreads (metastasizes), it commonly travels to the lumbar spine, causing persistent low back pain. Flank pain points to kidney issues, perineal pain and spasms point to prostatitis, and testicular lumps point to testicular cancer.

topic: Gastrointestinal Pathologies - Colon Cancer Presentation
question: A 57 year-old female has Colon Cancer. What are her symptoms?
options: lassitude, weakness, anorexia, intermittent diarrhea, steatorrhea, weight loss, rash
anorexia and early satiety, dysphagia, vomiting, weight loss, epigastric pain
alcoholism, recurrent attacks of epigastric pain, weight loss, glucose intolerance
bloody stools, anemia, abdominal ache and cramps, weight loss
correct: bloody stools, anemia, abdominal ache and cramps, weight loss
explanation: Colon cancer develops in the large intestine, where growing tumors often bleed slowly into the stool. This chronic blood loss causes anemia (low red blood cells), making the patient tired. As the tumor grows, it can block the bowel or irritate surrounding tissue, leading to abdominal cramps and pain. Systemic effects of cancer, like unintentional weight loss, are also common. Steatorrhea (fatty stools) points to malabsorption like Celiac disease, early satiety and dysphagia point to stomach issues, and alcoholism with epigastric pain points to chronic pancreatitis.

topic: Clinical Assessment - Valgus stress test
question: With the patient supine and the knee slightly flexed, you move the thigh about 30 degrees laterally to the side of the treatment table. You place one hand against the lateral knee to stabilize the femur and you place the other hand around the medial side of the ankle. With the hand on the lateral side of the knee, push medially against the knee and pull laterally at the ankle joint to open the knee on the medial side. This describes the
explanation: This test is also called the Abduction Stress Test. Pain or a gap in the medial joint line indicates that the medial ligaments are lax and there can possibly be a tear in the medial collateral ligament (MCL). The MCL is a band of tissue on the medial side of the knee connecting the femur with the tibia. The MCL prevents the knee from bending inward. In an MCL injury or tear to the medial collateral ligament, there can be pain, stiffness, swelling, tenderness along the inside of the knee, and feeling that the knee may give away, lock, or catch when the knee is under stress. Most knee injuries involve the MCL (medial collateral ligament).

topic: Clinical Assessment - Musculoskeletal Red Flags
question: Which of the following is a red flag that needs to be investigated before acupuncture is initiated?
options: A 50 year-old woman complains of an insidious onset of pain that affects the knee after walking
A 40 year-old man complains of immediate pain of the knee after kneeling for 2 hours at work
A 23 year-old runner receives immediate pain associated with the inability to weight bear on the right foot after running 3/4 of a marathon
An 18 year-old runner receives immediate pain of his right ankle after running a half marathon
correct: A 23 year-old runner receives immediate pain associated with the inability to weight bear on the right foot after running 3/4 of a marathon
explanation: In orthopedic assessment, the inability to bear weight on a limb after an injury or intense exertion is a major red flag. It strongly points to a bone fracture or severe ligament tear that requires immediate medical imaging (like an X-ray) and medical evaluation before starting acupuncture. Mild pain after kneeling, chronic knee pain after walking, or general ankle soreness without weight-bearing loss are typical overuse issues that do not require an immediate emergency referral.

topic: Clinical Assessment - Red Flag Headaches (SNOOP Mnemonic)
question: Which of the following is a mnemonic used to evaluate red flag headache cases?
explanation: The SNOOP mnemonic helps doctors quickly remember red flag warning signs for dangerous headaches. It stands for Systemic symptoms (like fever or cancer), Neurologic deficits (like weakness or confusion), Onset that is sudden (thunderclap), Older age of onset (new headaches after age 50), and Pattern changes (a headache that gets progressively worse). SOAP is a note-taking format, while 10 S's and SAD REP are not headache tools.

topic: Pharmacology - BPH Medications
question: A 52 year-old male has Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH). Treatment can include
explanation: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) is treated with two main types of drugs: Alpha-blockers like Flomax relax the prostate muscles so urine flows easier right away, while 5-alpha reductase inhibitors like Proscar and Avodart shrink the enlarged prostate over time. Therefore, Flomax, Proscar, and Avodart are all valid BPH treatments. Suprax is an antibiotic used for infections, not BPH.

topic: Pharmacology - Anti-infective Medications (Trichomoniasis)
question: A 27 year old female has itching in the vulva. The diagnosis is trichomoniasis. The preferred treatment is
explanation: Trichomoniasis is a common sexually transmitted infection caused by a microscopic parasite (a protozoan). Metronidazole (Flagyl) is the specific antiparasitic drug that kills this microorganism and cures the infection. Doxycycline and Ciprofloxacin are antibiotics designed to fight bacteria, not parasites, and Pentamidine is used for specific fungal pneumonia in immune-compromised patients.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - MSK Physical Exam (Posterior Drawer Test)
question: Which test is most helpful in diagnosing posterior cruciate ligament integrity?
explanation: The Posterior Drawer Test is the primary physical exam test used to check if the posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) inside the knee is torn. With the knee bent at 90 degrees, the doctor pushes the shinbone backward; if it slides back too far, the PCL is injured. The Pivot Shift test checks the ACL, Apley's distraction test checks for meniscal or collateral ligament issues, and the Posterior Sag sign is an observation rather than a manual drawer test.

topic: Mini pill
question: The generic names for progestin contraceptive drugs all end with
explanation: Progestin contraceptive drugs all end with -trel. Examples are desogestrel. Etonogestrel. Levonorgestrel. Norgestrel.

topic: Gastrointestinal Pathologies - Celiac Sprue Treatment
question: A 22 year-old male has Celiac Sprue. What is the primary treatment?
explanation: Celiac Sprue (celiac disease) is an autoimmune reaction caused by gluten, a protein found in wheat, barley, and rye. When a person with celiac disease eats gluten, their immune system damages the lining of the small intestine. The primary treatment is a strict, lifelong gluten-free diet, which allows the gut to heal completely. Vitamin B supplements can help if the patient is deficient, anti-spasmodics only relieve cramps, and corticosteroids are only for rare severe cases.

topic: Decision-Making & Standard of Care - Psychological Referral Criteria
question: A mother brought her 17 year-old son, Jake, to be treated for depression which started one year earlier. She determined that he was depressed because of poor concentration at school and withdrawal from family members. His school grades went from Bs to Ds and Fs. The mother was asked to leave the room for a private conversation with Jake. During the interview, Jake said he found school boring and denied any problems at home or with friends. When asked about drugs he replied that he smoked marijuana once in a while. Jake made poor eye contact, seemed a little angry, and remorseful. Which action would you take?
options: refer mother and son to a psychologist
refer son to a 12 step program
correct: refer mother and son to a psychologist
explanation: When a teenager shows severe changes in behavior, social withdrawal, and a steep drop in school grades over a year, it points to a significant mental health condition like depression. The proper medical standard of care is to refer the patient and family to a psychologist or mental health specialist for professional evaluation. Tutoring only addresses the symptom of poor grades, a 12-step program is meant for severe drug addiction rather than occasional use, and treating with acupuncture alone without mental health oversight misses the primary psychological diagnosis.

topic: Federal Regulations - DEA Controlled Substance Schedules (Vicodin)
question: Vicodin is classified as
explanation: Vicodin is a combination of hydrocodone (an opioid painkiller) and acetaminophen. Because hydrocodone carries a high risk of abuse, addiction, and severe physical dependency, the U.S. DEA classified hydrocodone combination products as Schedule II controlled substances. Schedule I drugs have no medical use, Schedule III drugs have a lower risk of abuse (like codeine with Tylenol), and Schedule IV drugs have an even lower abuse risk (like anti-anxiety medications).

topic: Integration TCM + Biomed - Western Medications & TCM Patterns (Cipro)
question: A 32-year old female is prescribed Cipro (ciprofloxacin). Which TCM disharmony would most likely apply?
options: prolapsed uterus due to deficient yang qi
uterine bleeding due to excess heat
explanation: Cipro (ciprofloxacin) is a common antibiotic used primarily to treat bacterial infections of the urinary tract (UTIs). In Traditional Chinese Medicine, urinary infections and painful or blocked urination (retention) are classified as Damp-Heat in the Lower Burner (Bladder). Prolapsed organs relate to Qi deficiency, uterine bleeding to heat in the blood, and insomnia to Liver Fire, none of which are primary indications for Cipro.

topic: Endocrine Pathologies - Hypothyroidism / Myxedema Symptoms
question: What would an amenorrheic female patient with myxedema report as her symptom?
explanation: Myxedema is a severe form of hypothyroidism (low thyroid hormone levels). Because thyroid hormones set the body's metabolism and heat production, a severe deficiency slows everything down. This causes classic symptoms like cold intolerance (feeling cold when others are comfortable), weight gain, slowness, and menstrual irregularities such as amenorrhea (absence of periods). Sweating excessively and inability to sit still (restlessness) are symptoms of hyperthyroidism (overactive thyroid), not myxedema.

topic: Federal Regulations - HIPAA Medical Record Access & Consent
question: Other than healthcare personnel, who is authorized to access medical records?
options: Staff members who have it as part their job description
Staff members that the patient has agreed to in the consent form agreement
correct: Staff members who have it as part their job description
explanation: Medical records shall be secured in a designated locked area and accessible by staff who have appropriate authorization when access is necessary for job function.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Cranial Nerves (Extraocular Muscle Innervation)
question: Which Cranial Nerve innervates the superior oblique extraocular muscle?
explanation: The trochlear nerve (Cranial Nerve IV) specifically controls the superior oblique muscle of the eye, which pulls the eye downward and inward. A common medical memory trick is LR6-SO4-R3: Lateral Rectus is CN VI, Superior Oblique is CN IV, and the Rest of the eye muscles are CN III. CN V controls facial sensation and chewing, not eye movement.

topic: Pulmonary Pathologies - Pleuritic Chest Pain / Pleurisy Presentation
question: A 25-year old male presents with pain that is worse with deep breath respirations, has a pleural friction rub, and an abnormal chest x-ray. EKG is normal. There are no rales or rhonchi to auscultation of the lungs. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Pleuritic chest pain (pleurisy) is inflammation of the lining around the lungs. Its main hallmark is sharp chest pain that gets worse whenever the patient takes a deep breath or coughs. The classic physical exam sound for pleurisy is a "pleural friction rub," which sounds like sandpaper rubbing together as the lungs expand. Pneumonia would show wet lung sounds (rales or rhonchi), pneumothorax would cause missing breath sounds on one side, and a pulmonary embolism usually causes severe sudden shortness of breath with heart rate changes.

topic: Neurological Pathologies - Alzheimer's Disease Presentation
question: A 70 year-old female patient is brought to the office by her daughter. The daughter reports that her mother has not been herself lately because she no longer joins her friends for activities and does not take care of her personal hygiene. At home she fails to clean up, missing stains in the bathroom and kitchen and saying that she does not see them. The daughter reports that she has a down mood and is not interested in what is happening with the family. She often repeats the same stories over and over, asks the same questions, has been more forgetful, and has lost her house keys several times during the past two months. She no longer goes to her book club because of her poor concentration. The mother stays at home most of the time and watches television. She has had high cholesterol since she was 62. She reports normal sleep and appetite. She denies any tingling, numbness, speech impairment, problems with coordination or balance. She is currently on medication for cholesterol. Vital signs: BP 120/70; P 68; R 16; height 5 ft 4 inches; weight 134 lbs; BMI 23.2. Vision screening was normal. Mental Status Exam: she is alert and oriented to the environment but is unsure of what month and day it is. Registration of objects was 3 of 3. Recall at 5 minutes was only 2 of 3. She was unable to spell the word "world" backward. The MMSE score was 18 out of 30. An MRI shows both parietal and hippocampus atrophy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disorder that causes gradual loss of memory, reasoning, and ability to care for oneself. Key features here include progressive memory loss, loss of daily living skills, an abnormal MMSE mental exam score (18 out of 30), and characteristic brain shrinking (atrophy) in the hippocampus (the memory center) and parietal lobe on MRI scan. Mild cognitive impairment leaves daily functions intact, vascular dementia follows sudden strokes with physical nerve symptoms, and depression does not cause physical brain atrophy on MRI.

topic: Myocardial Infarction
question: A patient with a history of myocardial infarctions complains of chest pain and dizziness. Which of the following signs can indicate the early stage of a cardiogenic shock and require urgent referral and care?
explanation: Within the context of a heart attack, an early stage of cardiogenic shock shows as a rapid (140 to 250 bpm) and strong pulse. This type of pulse rate is an indication of superventricular tachycardia or atrial fibrillation. This type of pulse is experienced by the patient as a pounding heart (palpitations). This is high priority red flag. A very weak and slow pulse can occur at a later stage of cardiogenic shock. It indicates that the heart is slowly ceasing to function as a result of pumping too hard. This is also high priority red flag. Cardiogenic shock is caused by the failure of the pumping action of the heart to circulate blood, either caused by heart muscle damage arising from a heart attack, heart valve problems, congestive heart failure, or irregular heart rhythm. Simply stated, cardiogenic shock is caused by the inadequate pumping of the heart due to heart disease or heart attack. Symptoms of cardiogenic shock Symptoms include: fainting, extremely low blood pressure, cold feet and hands, difficulty breathing, chest pain, pale skin, confusion, rapid breathing rate. The normal respiratory rate for an adult can be, according to different sources, 12 to 16 or 10 to 20 breaths per minute. In the initial stage of shock, there can be a rapid and respiratory rate as the body tries to compensate for the lack of blood flow to the body. There can also be a strong pulse but in the in the early stages but in the later stages of shock the pulse will be weak. For an adult, a resting pulse rate between 60 and 100 is considered normal. For an athlete a rate of 40 can be normal. A very slow pulse rate of 40 to 50 is a red flag for shock due to heart failure or arrhythmia. A severe heart attack that initiates the shock response can proceed to heart failure. That is, what started with a rapid heart rate in the early stages of shock, due to a heart attack, can progress to a very low heart rate when the heart attacks worsens into heart failure. Cardiogenic shock can occur very quickly following a heart attack (chest pressure, shoulder pain, pain along jawline, SOB, dizziness, nausea). Cardiogenic shock is the leading cause of death for patients with acute heart attack who reach the hospital alive.

topic: Nutrients & Supplements - Antacid Toxicities & Side Effects
question: What are the common side effects of excessive use of OTC antacids that contain calcium, aluminum, phosphorus, or magnesium?
options: constipation, muscle symptoms, respiratory symptoms, weak bones
muscle symptoms, respiratory symptoms, weak bones, jaundice
weak bones, jaundice, constipation, muscle symptoms
constipation, muscle symptoms, jaundice, respiratory symptom
correct: constipation, muscle symptoms, respiratory symptoms, weak bones
explanation: Overusing over-the-counter antacids leads to mineral imbalances in the body. Calcium and aluminum cause constipation. Electrolyte shifts from magnesium or calcium disrupt muscle control, causing muscle weakness or spasms. Severe blood chemistry changes can slow down breathing (respiratory symptoms), while aluminum binding to phosphate robs bones of essential strength, leading to weak bones. Jaundice involves liver breakdown or bile blockage, not antacid overuse.

topic: Endocrine Pathologies - Graves' vs. Hashimoto's Thyroiditis
question: In Graves' disease the immune system attacks the thyroid gland causing __________________. In Hashimoto's thyroiditis the immune system attacks the thyroid gland causing __________________.
explanation: Graves' disease and Hashimoto's thyroiditis are both autoimmune thyroid conditions, but they have opposite effects on hormone production. In Graves' disease, antibodies overstimulate the thyroid gland, causing it to produce too much hormone (hyperthyroidism). In Hashimoto's thyroiditis, the immune system destroys thyroid tissue over time, causing the gland to produce too little hormone (hypothyroidism).

topic: Pharmacology - Asthma Medications (Beta-2 Agonists)
question: Which of the following are beta-agonist drugs used during an asthma attack?
explanation: Beta-agonists like Ventolin (albuterol), Alupent (metaproterenol), and Brethine (terbutaline) work quickly during an asthma attack by relaxing the smooth muscles surrounding the airways to open them up so the patient can breathe. Zyflo (zileuton) is a leukotriene inhibitor used for long-term asthma prevention, not a fast-acting beta-agonist used during an acute attack.

topic: Decision-Making & Standard of Care - Suicide Risk Assessment & Emergency Protocols
question: A 30 year-old male requested acupuncture treatment for constipation and abdominal pain which was relieved with a bowel movement. The constipation started one week ago when his girlfriend moved out after discovering that he was seeing another woman. He said that he was depressed about it. When asked if he had thoughts of suicide or had plans to hurt himself, he answered in the affirmative. During the interview the patient sighed a lot and made poor eye contact. The abdominal examination was normal. Which action would you take?
options: have patient sign "no-harm" contract with a semi-urgent referral to the PCP
have friend or family member drive patient to psychiatric clinic
call 911 for emergency transport to psychiatric clinic
semi-urgent (next day) referral to the PCP
correct: have patient sign "no-harm" contract with a semi-urgent referral to the PCP
explanation: The red flag is a pessimistic, hopeless, and helpless patient. Major depression is assumed present until proven otherwise. The type of referral depends on the risk of suicide and the ability to pay for services. Psychological emergency services should be activated right away for patients who have plans to commit suicide and refuse to sign a "no-harm" contract which states that they will not seek to harm themselves directly or indirectly while waiting to receive psychological support services for the depression. The clinician also signs the contract. Patients with strong thoughts of suicides but no plans for suicide should receive a semi-urgent referral to the PCP who can either deal with the issue directly or do a further referral for psychological services. Patients with fleeting suicidal thoughts or no suicide thoughts should be referred on a timely basis to their PC.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Urinalysis Interpretation (Nitrites)
question: In the Urinalysis test which urine constituent indicates the possible presence of bacterial infection somewhere in the urinary tract?
explanation: Many bacteria that cause urinary tract infections (like E. coli) produce an enzyme that turns normal nitrates in urine into nitrites. Finding nitrites in a urinalysis is a key sign that a bacterial infection is present in the bladder or kidneys. Ketones show fat burning from starvation or diabetes, bilirubin indicates liver or gallbladder issues, and urobilinogen relates to red blood cell breakdown or liver function.

topic: Infection Control - Skin Lesions & Needling Contraindications
question: A patient has a suppurating skin lesion that is undiagnosed by a western physician. What action is appropriate by the acupuncturist?
options: provide acupuncture treatment for the skin disorder
do not needle the area and its surrounding skin
delay treatment until a western assessment
provide herb treatment for the skin disorder
correct: delay treatment until a western assessment
explanation: This is to identify possible MRSA (Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcous Aureus). Do not start acupuncture treatment until appropriate antibiotics are given to the patient.

topic: Biomedical Sciences - Renal Physiology (Daily Glomerular Filtration Volume)
question: About how much blood do healthy adult kidneys process on an average day?
explanation: Every day, healthy adult kidneys filter approximately 180 liters (about 45 to 50 gallons) of fluid out of the blood through microscopic filters called nephrons. However, the body reabsorbs almost 99% of that fluid back into the bloodstream, which is why a person only produces about 1.5 to 2 liters of urine per day. Values like 30 liters are far too low, while 300 or 800 liters are much higher than normal physiological filtering capacity.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Neuro Dermatomes (Lumbosacral Radiculopathy)
question: Which nerve root involvement is associated with sensory loss at the lateral side of the foot and small toe?
explanation: Sensory mapping (dermatomes) helps pinpoint spinal nerve root compression. The S1 nerve root supplies sensory feeling to the outer (lateral) edge of the foot and the small (fifth) toe. In contrast, the L4 nerve root covers the inner (medial) side of the foot, the L5 nerve root covers the top (dorsum) of the foot and the big toe, and L3 covers the thigh and knee.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Diagnostic/Lab Tests (TRH Test)
question: Which of the following thyroid-related tests helps to differentiate between primary and secondary hypothyroidism?
explanation: Primary hypothyroidism means the thyroid gland itself is damaged, while secondary hypothyroidism means the pituitary gland in the brain is failing to tell the thyroid to work. Giving a dose of TRH (Thyrotropin-Releasing Hormone) tests how the pituitary responds. If the pituitary is healthy (primary hypothyroidism), TRH triggers a huge surge in TSH. If the pituitary is damaged (secondary hypothyroidism), giving TRH produces no TSH response. Total T3 and T4 only show hormone levels, not where the defect is located.

topic: Gynecologic & Reproductive Pathologies - Endometriosis Presentation
question: During her period, a 39 year-old female experiences heavy menstrual flow, deep pelvic pain, painful urination, and painful intercourse. The pelvic exam reveals abnormal tissue growth between the uterus and rectum that is painful when touched. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Endometriosis occurs when tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside the uterus, such as on the ovaries, bladder, or space between the uterus and rectum. During menstruation, this tissue bleeds and swells, causing deep pelvic pain, heavy flow, painful urination, and painful intercourse (dyspareunia). Finding tender, abnormal tissue nodules during a pelvic exam is a classic sign. PID causes acute infection with fever and discharge, PCOS causes hormonal issues like missed periods and excess hair, and fibroids are non-tender muscle tumors inside the uterine wall.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Neuro Dermatomes (Cervical Radiculopathy)
question: The sensation for C5 is
options: Medial forearm, ring and small finger
Lateral forearm, thumb and index finger
explanation: The C5 nerve root supplies feeling (sensation) to the skin on the upper, outer side of the arm (the lateral arm around the deltoid muscle). The lateral forearm, thumb, and index finger are supplied by C6; the middle finger is supplied by C7; and the medial forearm, ring, and small finger are supplied by C8 and T1.

topic: Patient Hx & Physical Exam - Diagnostic/Lab Tests (Lipid Panel)
question: Generally, what LDL cholesterol level is considered high-risk for an adult?
explanation: LDL is often called 'bad cholesterol' because high amounts cause plaque buildup in arteries. Medical guidelines categorize LDL levels under 100 mg/dL as optimal, 130-159 mg/dL as borderline high, and levels greater than 160 mg/dL as high risk for heart disease and stroke. A level of 200 mg/dL or above applies to total cholesterol categories, not LDL alone.

topic: Risk Management & Safety - Seizure Emergency Protocols (Calling 911)
question: Which type of patient with seizures requires calling 911?
options: patient has diabetes, patient is pregnant
patient with a two minute seizure, patient is elderly
patient with a two minute seizure, patient has diabetes, patient is pregnant
patient is elderly, patient has diabetes, patient is pregnant
correct: patient is elderly, patient has diabetes, patient is pregnant
explanation: This is the most complete and accurate answer. Most seizures last only a few minutes with the person recovering fully without any complications. But if the seizures last more than five minutes or the patient has multiple seizures in a row then calling 911 is necessary. There are other circumstances which necessitate calling 911 when a patient has seizures. This includes patients with diabetes, pregnant patients, and the elderly. Also call 911 if the seizure was due to high fever, it was the first ever seizure for the patient or the patient is unresponsive and not breathing or gasping for air after the seizure is over or the patient was injured as a result of the seizure.

topic: Decision-Making & Standard of Care - Red Flags & Referral Protocols (Hemoptysis & Localized Wheeze)
question: A 40 year-old female presented with a one-month history of progressively worsening cough with occasional bright-red blood in the sputum. The morning before the appointment she coughed up about 1/4 teaspoon of blood. She denies having fever or an upper respiratory infection. Physical examination revealed a wheeze on the left side. Which action would you take?
options: timely (1-2 weeks) referral to primary care physician
semi-urgent (next day) referral to primary care physician
provide acupuncture treatment for the cough and wheezing
correct: semi-urgent (next day) referral to primary care physician
